items.title: How to Track the Midterms Results
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. I have a confession to make: As a political journalist, I hate Election Day. It’s a day when it’s too late to report or write anything that will inform readers or illuminate the campaign, but it’s also too soon to have the results and analyze them. That leaves me with nothing but nervous energy and nowhere to channel it. Perhaps you feel some of this anxiety too—especially given how high-stakes elections feel for Americans of all political views. ( STAT reported last week that hospitals see more heart-attack cases right after Election Day.) Having a plan for how to absorb the news this evening is one way to soothe your nerves. First, don’t try to follow everything. Leave the Magic Walls, Big Boards, and comprehensive tracking of House races to John King and Steve Kornacki. You don’t need to worry about what’s going on in, say, Florida’s Twenty-Seventh District with 17 percent of the vote counted. The first polls close at 6 p.m. eastern today, but many of the states with pivotal elections won’t stop voting until 8 or 9 p.m. eastern; Alaskan polling locations close at 1 a.m. eastern. Pick just a few races that are of particular interest to you—either because you live somewhere with a contested race or because you’re especially interested in some candidate. You can also stay focused on the big ideas and stakes by watching The Atlantic ’s livestream, featuring Tom Nichols, David Frum, Anne Applebaum, and more. That starts at 9 p.m. eastern on TheAtlantic.com and on our app. Several races might be good indicators of where the rest of the election is headed. (I hope needless to say, but don’t pay attention to the early exit polls , whatever you do.) The first of the major Senate polls to close will be at 7:30 in Ohio, where the GOP incumbent Jon Husted—he of the supposedly callipygian physique —is facing off against the Democratic challenger Sherrod Brown. Maine and most of Michigan, also pivotal Senate races, close at 8, though Democratic hopes will ride on turnout in Detroit, where vote counting was very slow in 2020 and 2024, so don’t bet on an early call there. But we might get hints from other races. In New Hampshire, Democrat Chris Pappas is favored over Republican John Sununu, but if the result is close, it might be a reason for Democrats to temper hopes. The same is true in Minnesota, where Democrat Peggy Flanagan is expected to hold off Republican Michele Tafoya. (If either Democrat loses, expect panic left of center.) In South Carolina, the short-term Republican incumbent, Darline Graham, seems to have the edge—major forecasters rate the race as leaning Republican—but if Democrat Annie Andrews is close, that would suggest strong Democratic results elsewhere. (If Andrews wins, it will be Republicans panicking.) Second, remember that there’s no such thing as a final result on Election Night. Unfortunately, reporters and anchors tend to discuss results coming in from local officials as though the votes are being cast in real time, saying that a candidate is “pulling ahead” and the like. Race calls from networks or the Associated Press are merely judgments about who will win, not binding in any way. In fact, races are complete only when officials certify them, and the order in which votes are counted is irrelevant to the outcome. This is especially important because of a phenomenon known as the “ blue shift ”: For a variety of reasons, including the prevalence of Democratic voters in urban centers that have more votes and count more slowly, Democratic votes tend to be fully tallied later. The result is that an election that looks more favorable to Republicans based on early returns may turn out to be less so. Although President Trump has claimed blue shifts are evidence of fraud, this is not true. The idea that no outcome is valid until all votes are counted might seem intuitive, but it is lost even on some members of the Supreme Court. Justice Brett Kavanaugh has worried about a scenario in which “thousands of absentee ballots flow in after election day and potentially flip the results of an election.” But this isn’t the case at all—there’s no result to flip until those ballots have been tallied. Nonetheless, his colleague Samuel Alito wrote in a June dissent in Watson v. Republican National Committee that “allowing absentee ballots to pour in over the days and weeks after election day, by which point preliminary election returns are being publicly reported,” might risk “undermining the public’s confidence in election integrity.” Maybe these misunderstandings would be rarer if Supreme Court justices weren’t encouraging them. Finally, and relatedly, keep in mind that we may not really know how the election turned out for days, or even weeks. In 2018, polling predicted a “blue wave” for Democrats, but on the night of the election, their victory seemed modest —certainly short of some of the most favorable predictions. Not every race was counted, though. Over the following 10 days, more and more races were called for Democrats, eventually producing the party’s biggest gain since Watergate . The outcomes of some races will not be clear tonight or tomorrow, and when they eventually are, they may not break entirely or even predominantly for either party. The fact is that we don’t know. That uncertainty may feel uncomfortable, but it beats putting a lot of emotion into a result that isn’t real. Related: Brace for the blue shift ( From 2020 ) The Trump aide trying to stop a blue wave

items.title: Gombe ASUU rejects salary arrears, threatens fresh strike
items.description: …Union seeks NEC approval to resume suspended action over CATA, outstanding payments By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Gombe State University (GSU) branch, has rejected the salary arrears paid by the university management under the new salary structure, describing the amount as inadequate and below members’ entitlements. The union also announced that it would commence what it termed active non-compliance from November 4, 2026, until all academic staff receive their October salaries in full. The resolutions were reached at the branch congress held on November 3, 2026, where members reviewed the implementation of the 2025 ASUU-Federal Government agreement and the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) reached with the university management. In a statement jointly signed by the branch Chairman, Dr Mustapha Shehu Shehu, and Secretary, Dr Aliyu Umar Shelleng, the congress expressed dissatisfaction with the management’s implementation of the agreements, particularly the payment of salary arrears and other outstanding entitlements. The union said the amount paid as arrears under the new salary structure did not reflect the actual entitlements of its members and was therefore unacceptable. It consequently rejected the payment and demanded the immediate settlement of all outstanding obligations owed to academic staff. The congress also disclosed that it had sought approval from the union’s National Executive Council (NEC) to resume its suspended strike should the outstanding arrears not be correctly calculated and paid. The development raises concerns over industrial relations at the university, with the union’s resolutions signalling a possible escalation of its dispute with the management. ASUU said its demands remained the full payment of October 2026 salaries and the correct calculation and payment of arrears due to its members under the new salary structure. The post Gombe ASUU rejects salary arrears, threatens fresh strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pro-Tinubu solidarity march held in Ebonyi
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki A group of supporters of President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday staged solidarity marches across parts of Ebonyi State, ahead of the 2027 presidential election, in what organisers described as a response to alleged anti-Tinubu protests. The protesters, estimated by the organisers at about 20,000, marched through parts of the state, chanting solidarity songs and carrying placards with inscriptions such as “Tinubu Beyond 2027”, “Tinubu Must Stay” and “We Believe in Tinubu”. They also expressed support for Tinubu, Governor Francis Nwifuru and the All Progressives Congress (APC). Addressing the protesters in Abakaliki, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, thanked them for demonstrating their support for the President. Umahi commended the protesters for conducting the march peacefully, alleging that some political opponents were sponsoring anti-Tinubu demonstrations to shore up their declining popularity. He said the opposition lacked direction and issues with which to challenge the President, arguing that Tinubu’s reforms and policies had placed the country on the path to growth. The minister also faulted those organising protests against the President, saying they were disregarding the administration’s efforts to reposition the country. The leader of the protest, under the aegis of Ebonyi United Forum, Comrade Chinedu Nwali, said the group took to the streets in Abakaliki and other parts of the state to express its opposition to what he described as distractions by opposition elements against Tinubu’s administration. Nwali said the march was also intended to sensitise residents, particularly youths, to what he described as the gains recorded by the President. He warned that the group would resist attempts to undermine the administration of Tinubu, as well as that of Nwifuru and Umahi. “If other states are sitting on the fence, we Ebonyians are not going to sit on the fence. We must make our stand known because we are people who show appreciation for the numerous projects Mr President has used our son to execute in the South-East and Nigeria in general,” he said. Nwali described the march as a demonstration of Ebonyi’s support for Tinubu’s re-election, adding that the group would oppose what it considered political distractions. He also defended Umahi against criticism over his support for Tinubu, saying the minister was entitled to his political convictions. The post Pro-Tinubu solidarity march held in Ebonyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Experts advocate renewables, microgrids to tackle power crisis
items.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for increased investment in renewable energy and microgrids to complement the national grid and address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges. They made the call in separate interviews with Vanguard on the sidelines of the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit at Landmark, Lagos. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said Nigeria needed to accelerate the adoption of renewable energy, particularly solar power, noting that the national grid could not meet the country’s growing electricity demand. He said renewable energy offered an opportunity to expand access to electricity, especially for businesses and households seeking more reliable power supply. “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Renewable is a major aspect of Nigeria’s power sector. Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free,” he said. Alankar said the increasing demand for decentralised electricity was driving the development of systems that integrate solar power, battery storage, generators and the national grid. He said the company’s solutions were designed to improve fuel efficiency, optimise battery performance and maximise the use of solar energy. “The priority should be mostly on renewables rather than fossil fuels. Our whole mindset is based on the same concept that renewables should be more than fossil fuels,” he added. Also speaking, Executive Director of Delmira Power Solutions, Dr Moriam Jagun, identified frequent grid collapses as a major challenge, saying renewable energy could provide alternative electricity sources for homes and businesses. She said her company was the authorised channel partner for DEIF products in Nigeria, adding that the firm provided power systems for coordinating, protecting and monitoring electricity generation and distribution. According to her, the solutions are applicable to both land-based and marine power systems. The Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, also stressed the importance of reliable electricity to industrialisation and economic development. He said the company was expanding its DEIF franchise from land-based applications to the marine sector in Nigeria, with plans to strengthen its presence in the Nigerian and wider African markets. “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels,” Ayodele said. He added that DEIF solutions could remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources, including the national grid, solar photovoltaic systems, generators and batteries. According to him, integrating the different sources could help provide more reliable electricity to industries and households while reducing energy costs. The post Experts advocate renewables, microgrids to tackle power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Última hora del accidente de trenes de Urda, en Toledo, en directo | Puente defiende la seguridad de la línea Madrid-Sevilla: “No es una infraestructura ni abandonada ni olvidada”
items.description: El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha defendido este martes en el Congreso que la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla “no es una infraestructura ni abandonada ni olvidada” y ha recordado que su Gobierno puso en marcha un plan de renovación de 780 millones de euros. Puente ha relatado además que el centro de control de Adif en Atocha autorizó al AVE implicado en el accidente de Urda (Toledo) a reanudar la circulación en marcha normal, pese a la caída del sistema de seguridad LZB y a que había un tren de Iryo detenido más adelante. El AVE recorrió unos 25 kilómetros a más de 160 kilómetros por hora hasta alcanzar al Iryo a las 8.53. El accidente ha dejado 69 muertos y alrededor de 200 heridos, 40 de ellos aún hospitalizados. La portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, ha replicado al ministro que su responsabilidad “no es explicar accidentes mortales” sino evitarlos. “Es incompetente e incapaz de empatizar con el dolor ajeno”, ha zanjado. PP, Vox, PNV y Junts, que suman 35 de los 69 puestos de la Diputación Permanente, exigen la dimisión de Puente. Por su parte, el comité de empresa de Adif ha acordado una huelga para el 17 de noviembre por la seguridad ferroviaria, aunque todavía no está formalmente convocada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Football: décès de l’attaquant espagnol Jesús de Miguel après un violent choc en plein match
items.description: Le football espagnol est en deuil après le décès de Jesús de Miguel Alameda, attaquant du CD Tenerife, survenu ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, à l’âge de 30 ans. Le club a annoncé la triste nouvelle dans un communiqué officiel, précisant que le joueur a rendu son dernier souffle à 8 heures du matin, à l’hôpital, au lendemain d’une violente collision avec le gardien adverse lors d’un match de championnat. Le drame s’est produit le lundi 2 novembre 2026, à l’occasion de la rencontre entre le CD Tenerife et le FC Andorra, comptant pour la 12e journée du championnat espagnol de deuxième division. Dans les dernières secondes du temps additionnel, Jesús de Miguel est entré violemment en collision avec le gardien adverse, Jesús Owono, au cours d’une action disputée au milieu du terrain. À la suite de cet impact, l’attaquant espagnol a perdu connaissance. Rapidement pris en charge par les équipes médicales présentes sur place, il a été évacué en urgence vers un établissement hospitalier, où il a été admis en soins intensifs. La rencontre, qui s'est achevée sur le score de 2-2, a été interrompue à la suite de cet incident. Malgré les soins prodigués, l’état de santé du joueur s’est aggravé au cours de la nuit. Selon le communiqué du CD Tenerife, Jesús de Miguel Alameda est décédé ce mardi à 8 heures, à l’hôpital où il avait été admis après le choc. À la suite de cette tragédie, la Fédération royale espagnole de football a annoncé la suspension des rencontres programmées ce mardi, en signe de deuil. De son côté, le FC Andorra, ainsi que plusieurs acteurs du monde footballistique, ont exprimé leur profonde tristesse et adressé leurs condoléances à la famille du défunt et au CD Tenerife. À seulement 30 ans, Jesús de Miguel disparaît dans des circonstances particulièrement tragiques, laissant le football espagnol sous le choc. Un match de championnat s'est ainsi transformé en un drame qui plonge ses proches, son club et toute la communauté footballistique dans la douleur. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Football: décès de l’attaquant espagnol Jesús de Miguel après un violent choc en plein match est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. items.title: Tanger Med : une cargaison de 971 kg de cocaïne saisie dans un conteneur frigorifique
items.description: Une opération conjointe de contrôle aux frontières, de la police et des services douaniers a permis de déjouer, mardi 3 novembre, une tentative de trafic international de stupéfiants au port Tanger Med. Les autorités ont saisi 971 kilogrammes de cocaïne dissimulés dans un conteneur frigorifique à bord d’un navire battant pavillon d’un pays d’Amérique latine. Selon les premières informations communiquées, la drogue était dissimulée sous forme de plaquettes à l’intérieur d’un conteneur frigorifique transporté à bord d’un navire battant pavillon d’un pays d’Amérique latine. Les premiers éléments de l’enquête ont permis de retracer l’itinéraire du conteneur. Celui-ci aurait quitté un port brésilien et devait rejoindre un port situé en Afrique de l’Ouest. La cargaison a ainsi été interceptée lors de son passage par Tanger Med. Une enquête judiciaire a été ouverte par le service préfectoral de la police judiciaire de Tanger, sous la supervision du parquet compétent. Les investigations visent à déterminer l’ensemble des circonstances de cette opération et à identifier les personnes ainsi que les réseaux criminels impliqués dans cette tentative de trafic international. Le Bureau central national d’Interpol à Rabat, relevant de la DGSN, a également été chargé d’activer les mécanismes de coopération et de coordination internationales afin de remonter la filière et d’identifier les ramifications éventuelles du réseau à l’étranger. Cette saisie intervient dans un contexte de renforcement des opérations de contrôle et de lutte contre les circuits internationaux de trafic de stupéfiants transitant par les voies maritimes. The post Tanger Med : une cargaison de 971 kg de cocaïne saisie dans un conteneur frigorifique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Don’t cause crisis in Obi’s camp, OK Movement warns NDC, Obidients
items.description: … As Camp faces setback amid rift By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AS Campaigns have begun ahead of 2027 general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has warned the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement not to cause friction in the camp of the NDC Presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Recall that crisis had last month reared its head between the leadership of the party and the support group when the OK Movement unveiled its presidential campaign council and the leadership of the party immediately took a swipe at the development as it rejected the composition of the Campaign Council. The NDC maintained that the role of support groups should be limited to supporting the party and its candidates, rather than assuming the functions of a political party. The OK Movement on its part, resisted the NDC’s position, saying it had a mandate to ensure that Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso were elected in 2027. This led to strained relations between the two groups. Reacting to the development, the United Kingdom Coordinator of the OK Movement, Adebayo Brown, on Tuesday accused leaders of the NDC PCC and the Obidient Movement of encouraging divisions among groups associated with Peter Obi’s 2027 presidential ambition. Brown who urged the leaders to stop what he described as unnecessary political disputes, pleaded with them to focus on mobilising Nigerians, strengthening grassroots structures and preparing for the 2027 general elections, Adebayo Brown has accused the Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, Moses Paul, and the Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, of allegedly allowing political disagreements to distract them from their organisational responsibilities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Brown said the two individuals should concentrate on rebuilding political structures, strengthening grassroots mobilisation and campaigning for the party’s candidates rather than engaging in what he described as unnecessary personal and political disputes. Brown who expressed concern over what he described as the continued targeting of the National Director-General of the OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, by individuals expected to provide leadership within their respective organisations, however questioned the relevance of repeated claims by the Obidient Movement Coordinator that former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, had dissociated themselves from the OK Movement The statement is titled, ” Joblessnesss , Oblessness and lack of Leadership Capacity. “ Brown ‘s statement read, Two appointments have been given to individuals who now appear more interested in political disputes than in the responsibilities of their offices: one as Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and another as Director General of the NDC. “Ordinarily, one would expect people entrusted with such responsibilities to demonstrate a sense of urgency, focusing their energy on organising, mobilising, and campaigning for the party’s candidates. With the 2027 general elections approaching, the task ahead demands strategic thinking, effective coordination, and grassroots mobilisation. “Unfortunately, rather than concentrating on these critical responsibilities, their attention appears to be directed towards the National Director General of the OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu. “With only 76 days to the general elections, one would expect serious minded leaders to be preoccupied with building structures, strengthening grassroots engagement, and preparing for the enormous responsibility of electoral mobilisation. Instead, MO continues to make claims that HE Peter Obi and HE Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso have dissociated themselves from the OK Movement. “The question is simple: how does this constant repetition of such claims contribute to the success of the party or the democratic aspirations of Nigerians? ” The strength of the OK Movement is rooted in its ideology, principles, and core values—not in the approval of individuals or the political positions they occupy. “MO should concentrate on the mandate entrusted to him: rebuilding, revitalising, and restructuring the Obidient Movement. This is an opportunity to demonstrate leadership, capacity, and organisational competence. The task deserves his full attention, not a diversion into unnecessary personal and political disagreements. “We recognise and respect the tenacity, capacity, and integrity of Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, National Director-General of the OK Movement, who has made significant sacrifices to build the movement into what it is today. “The journey has not been easy. He has invested considerable personal resources, time, energy, and commitment in the collective vision of the OK Movement. In the face of challenges, he has continued to stand for justice, equity, fairness, and the principles upon which the movement was established. “It is important to make one thing absolutely clear: Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu is a successful businessman and a committed advocate of workers’ interests. His commitment to the movement should not be misrepresented as a pursuit of personal gain. “Those who appear uncomfortable with his independence must understand that the OK Movement is an organisation built around principles and a collective vision, not the personal ambitions of any individual. “Furthermore, the Coordinator of the Obidient Movement does not automatically speak for HE Peter Obi, nor can he unilaterally determine or represent the interests of HE Peter Obi and HE Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. Such positions should be established through clear and verifiable communication, not personal assertions.” Warning that the divisive rhetoric must stop, Adebayo Brown said, ” For the avoidance of doubt, the OK Movement and the Obidient Movement are not enemies. Neither is the OK Movement in conflict with the NDC. We have a common democratic challenge ahead, and the priority should be mobilising Nigerians, strengthening political structures, and working towards credible elections in 2027. “MO should therefore focus on the enormous responsibility before him. Rebuilding the Obidient Movement, strengthening its grassroots structures, and mobilising supporters require serious work, strategic planning, and measurable results. That is where his energy should be directed. “Nigeria is bigger than any individual, and the struggle for democracy is greater than personal disagreements. “We have advised Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu to disregard these distractions and remain focused on the work of building the OK Movement, strengthening its structures, and contributing meaningfully to the defence of Nigeria’s democracy. “The OK Movement will not be distracted, intimidated, or defined by the opinions of individuals. Our commitment remains justice, equity, fairness, credible elections, and a better Nigeria. The time for division is over. The time to work is now.” ENDS The post Don’t cause crisis in Obi’s camp, OK Movement warns NDC, Obidients appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: When applause replaces discernment
items.description: There is something about the recent exchanges among some prominent Ghanaian religious leaders that deserves more attention than it is receiving. The focus has largely been on what one pastor said about other prophets, who has responded, who has taken offence and who has insulted whom. But I believe we are overlooking an equally important part of the story: the people sitting in the congregations, listening, clapping, cheering and sometimes appearing visibly delighted as their pastors attack fellow ministers from the pulpit. My question is simple: Who are those clapping? What exactly are they celebrating? Is it the defence of Christianity? Is it the correction of wrongdoing within the prophetic ministry? Or is it simply the pleasure of watching their pastor insult another man of God? The distinction matters. The Otabil controversy and the bigger question Pastor Mensa Otabil, Founder and General Overseer of the International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), recently made strong remarks about people who identify themselves as prophets in Ghana. He questioned the spiritual authenticity and lifestyles of many of them, alleging that some engage in sexual misconduct, make false claims and practise activities he described as occultism, spiritism and necromancy. He also challenged those who consider themselves genuine prophets to speak against individuals whose conduct, in his view, damages the credibility of the prophetic ministry. Importantly, he clarified that he believes in the prophetic gift; his concern was about practices being presented as biblical prophecy when he considers them inconsistent with Christian teaching. I do not claim to possess the spiritual authority, powers or right to pronounce on who is a genuine prophet and who is not. That judgement is not mine to make. Neither am I in a position to verify the percentage of prophets Otabil was referring to. His reported observations should not automatically be treated as established statistical facts. However, I agree with the central concern he has raised: there is a serious need for the Christian community to confront questionable conduct among people who occupy the pulpit and claim spiritual authority. It is not enough to profess Christianity, carry the title of pastor or prophet, command a large congregation and enjoy public recognition. The conduct of those who claim to represent God must be open to scrutiny. What has followed his remarks, however, is revealing. Some religious leaders have responded with sharp personal attacks, insults and statements challenging his own spiritual credentials. Among the reported reactions, Reverend Isaac Owusu Bempah criticised Otabil and made personal allegations, while Prophet Nigel Gaisie expressed disagreement and called for engagement and mentorship among ministers. People may disagree with Otabil. They are entitled to challenge his arguments, question his generalisations and defend the prophetic ministry. That is not the problem. The problem is the manner in which disagreement is sometimes expressed, particularly when personal insults replace reasoned engagement. But even more troubling is the reaction of some congregations. Why are members clapping? Imagine a preacher standing behind the pulpit, supposedly representing Christian values, using the opportunity to insult another pastor. He makes personal remarks, questions another person’s calling, attacks their character and uses language that would ordinarily be considered unacceptable in a civil conversation. The congregation responds with applause, laughter, shouting and cheering. What exactly is happening? Are the members listening to a sermon or watching a confrontation? Have they come to church to receive spiritual instruction or to participate in a public contest between religious personalities? And if the same preacher were to direct those insults at an ordinary member of the congregation, would the reaction be the same? This is the question I want members of such churches to confront honestly. When your pastor insults another man of God and you clap, what are you endorsing? Are you endorsing the substance of his argument, or are you celebrating his ability to humiliate someone else? When your pastor makes personal attacks rather than addressing the issues raised, do you consider that spiritual leadership? When he threatens to expose another minister or makes allegations that have not been substantiated, why does that generate excitement rather than caution? A church congregation should not become an audience that rewards every performance from the pulpit, regardless of its content. The pulpit carries responsibility. It should be a place for teaching, correction, reflection, spiritual guidance and the promotion of values. It should not become a platform for settling personal scores, displaying arrogance or entertaining members with insults directed at other religious leaders. Your pastor is not above scrutiny One of the worrying developments in some religious communities is the extent to which followers appear to have surrendered their independent judgement to the personalities leading their churches. A pastor says something, and members accept it. A prophet makes a declaration, and members celebrate it. A preacher attacks another minister, and the congregation cheers. Someone raises a legitimate question, and that person is immediately labelled an enemy of the church or an agent of spiritual opposition. At what point did religious loyalty become unquestioning personal loyalty to a preacher? A pastor is a human being entrusted with spiritual responsibilities. That position deserves respect, but it does not confer immunity from accountability. The title of Reverend, Apostle, Bishop or Prophet does not place anyone beyond criticism. Members must understand that defending Christianity does not mean defending every person who claims to represent it. Similarly, questioning a preacher’s conduct does not amount to questioning God. There is a dangerous confusion between faith in God and loyalty to a particular religious personality. When the two become indistinguishable, followers may begin to defend behaviour they would ordinarily condemn in any other setting. A person who insults, humiliates, intimidates or makes unsubstantiated allegations about others does not automatically become justified because the behaviour takes place inside a church. The congregation must be able to recognise that distinction. When applause becomes permission Applause may seem harmless. People clap for different reasons: excitement, agreement, encouragement or simply because everyone else is clapping. I am not suggesting that every person who applauds a preacher necessarily endorses everything that person says. But applause has consequences when it repeatedly rewards questionable conduct. When a preacher insults another minister or even members of the congregation and receives enthusiastic applause, the congregation may be reinforcing the idea that such behaviour is acceptable. When members cheer personal attacks, they help create an environment in which aggression becomes a form of religious entertainment. When they defend every statement made by their pastor, regardless of evidence or principle, they weaken the very accountability that religious institutions need. This is not merely a problem of individual behaviour. It is an institutional problem. Churches are institutions. They have leadership structures, responsibilities, resources, members and governing arrangements. They should therefore be guided by principles of accountability, transparency, fairness and responsible leadership. A congregation that never questions its leadership is not necessarily a congregation demonstrating strong faith. It may simply be one in which accountability has become difficult. The same members who applaud their pastor when he insults another may one day find themselves on the receiving end of similar treatment. What happens then? Will they still applaud? Will they still defend the behaviour? Or will they suddenly recognise that spiritual authority does not justify disrespect? Why do followers defend questionable conduct? We must also examine why some members become so invested in defending their pastors, even when the conduct in question deserves scrutiny. For some, the preacher has become the centre of their religious identity. Their loyalty is no longer simply to the church or its teachings but to the personality of the person leading it. Criticism of the preacher is therefore experienced as a personal attack. For others, there is the fear of being spiritually punished or rejected. They may have been taught, directly or indirectly, that questioning the pastor amounts to questioning God. Such an environment makes it difficult for members to raise concerns, even when they have legitimate reasons. There is also the issue of social and financial investment. People give their time, money and emotional commitment to their churches. They develop friendships, build relationships and sometimes organise their entire lives around the ministry. Admitting that a leader may have acted wrongly can be difficult because it raises uncomfortable questions about their own loyalty and judgement. But none of these reasons should justify abandoning personal responsibility. A believer should be able to respect a pastor while disagreeing with him. A member should be able to appreciate a ministry while questioning its practices. And a congregation should be able to defend the integrity of its church without automatically defending every action of its leader. The responsibility of the church member The Christian community must begin to take the responsibility of its members more seriously. Members should not measure the credibility of a preacher solely by the size of the congregation, the dramatic nature of the prophecies, the number of miracles claimed, the expensive lifestyle or the ability to command applause. They should pay attention to character, conduct, humility, truthfulness and accountability. They should ask whether the preacher’s teachings are consistent with the values he professes. They should be concerned about financial transparency and the treatment of members. They should question the use of fear, threats and extraordinary promises to influence people’s decisions. They should also distinguish between disagreement and misconduct. A minister has every right to defend his calling and challenge another person’s statements. But disagreement does not require insults, intimidation or unsubstantiated allegations. There is nothing unchristian about asking a question. There is nothing rebellious about demanding accountability. And there is nothing wrong with refusing to applaud conduct that contradicts the values one claims to believe in. Indeed, sometimes the most responsible thing a church member can do is remain silent when everyone else is clapping. The church must not reward what it should correct I do not expect all religious leaders to agree with Pastor Otabil. I do not expect every pastor or prophet to accept his assessment. The prophetic ministry, like other areas of Christian service, can be discussed, defended and critically examined. But if the debate is genuinely about protecting the integrity of Christianity, then the response should reflect the very values the church teaches. Let those who disagree make their arguments. Let them explain their understanding of prophecy, defend their ministry and challenge generalisations they consider unfair. But let the debate be conducted with dignity, evidence and respect. More importantly, let church members stop confusing the defence of a pastor with the defence of Christianity. A congregation should not be proud merely because its pastor can insult another preacher and command applause. It should be concerned about whether that pastor demonstrates the character, discipline and responsibility expected of someone entrusted with spiritual leadership. The question is not whether your pastor can speak forcefully. It is whether he can speak responsibly. So, who are those clapping? I return to my question. Who are those clapping when their pastor insults another man of God? Who are those cheering when personal attacks replace meaningful arguments? Who are those celebrating threats, humiliation and allegations that have not been established? Who are those who appear more interested in seeing another preacher disgraced than in hearing a message that strengthens their faith? What exactly are they teaching their children and younger members about respect, humility, truth and Christian conduct? Perhaps it is time for church members to understand that they are not merely spectators in the religious activities of their congregations. Their reactions help shape the culture of their churches. Their financial contributions sustain ministries. Their loyalty gives leaders influence. And their willingness to question or excuse misconduct can determine whether accountability is possible. A preacher who behaves irresponsibly must answer for his conduct. But congregations must also examine what they reward, what they tolerate and what they defend. I do not have the authority to determine who is a true prophet or a false prophet. But I believe every Christian has a responsibility to distinguish between spiritual leadership and personal misconduct. The next time your pastor stands behind the pulpit to insult another person, do not be in a hurry to clap. Ask yourself what you are celebrating. Because sometimes the problem is not only the person holding the microphone. It is also the congregation that keeps applauding. Dr. Michael Kubi Scholar-practitioner, author, governance consultant and lecturer, University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA). mocorn2013@gmail.com

items.title: Insecurity: Borno Police nab 103 suspected criminals
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has arrested 103 suspected criminals in connection to combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices. The arrests were carried out in Maiduguri metropolis between the months of October 29 to November 2nd, 2026, with support from its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit. This was disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Keneth Daso in a statement he signed on Tuesday. The statement reads partly: “In a sustained effort to rid Maiduguri metropolis of criminal elements and combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices, the Borno State Police Command, through its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit, has recorded a major operational breakthrough with the arrest of 103 suspects during a week-long township patrol and coordinated raid operations conducted between 29th October and 2nd November 2026. “The operations, carried out on the directives of the Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Abdulmajid, psc, involved a combined team of Police operatives and other relevant security agencies. “The joint operations focused on identified crime-prone areas and security hotspots across the metropolis, including Gwange, Santiago, Texaco, Ajari, Gadan Zare, Budum, Shehuri, Bulabulin, Abbaganaram, Baga Road, Gidan Dambe, UNIMAID 202 Housing Estate, Mairi Kuwait, Bakari, Zanneri, Polo, Giwa Barrack Area, Kwanan Yobe, Jiddari, Kaleri, Damboa Road, Circular and Moduganari, among other locations. “The operations resulted in the arrest of 103 suspects for offences bordering on public nuisance, possession and sale of illicit drugs, and possession of dangerous weapons. “The suspects are undergoing preliminary screening and investigation, while those found culpable will be prosecuted in accordance with the law”. Daso said. Items recovered include; 889 wraps of Indian hemp, 104 wraps of Erinmo, 7 packs of Colorado and 2 quantities of methamphetamine (Ice). Also recovered according to the statement are 8 bottles of Codeine syrup, 266 tablets of D5, 13 tablets of Diazepam, 11 tablets of Tramadol, 7 capsules of Tramadol and 300 capsules of Exole. Additionally Daso said, 12 tablets of Exole, 4 ice bunkers, 1 bottle of Methylene Chloride, popularly known as “Suck and Die”, 4 sharp knives, 1 cutlass. 16. 1 axe, 11 rounds of live ammunition, 3 sets of Shisha pots and 11 pieces of ice bulbs were recovered from the suspects. “The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Abdulmajid, psc, commended the operatives and collaborating security agencies for their commitment, vigilance and proactive approach to maintaining public safety. “He reaffirmed the Command’s resolve to sustain intelligence-led operations, intensify the fight against illicit drug activities and dismantle criminal hideouts and networks capable of threatening public peace and security. “The Command calls on members of the public to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by providing credible and timely information on suspicious activities, criminal hideouts and other security threats. Such information can be channelled through established Police communication platforms”. Daso stressed. Accordingly he said, the Borno State Police Command remains committed to protecting lives and property and ensuring a safer environment for all residents The post Insecurity: Borno Police nab 103 suspected criminals appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How Trump could interfere in US midterm elections
items.description: State officials who run US elections are braced for possible intervention by President Donald Trump’s administration in Tuesday’s midterms – fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavorable results. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to keep control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to “nationalize” voting in at least 15 places. The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical. The US Constitution gives the president no direct role in running elections, and courts have so far rebuffed the administration’s main legal challenges. Here are the key potential flashpoints: Who gets to vote The Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to obtain their voter registration lists, saying it needs them to find non-citizens. It has lost more than two dozen of those cases. It has also demanded that ballots be set aside from about 20,000 people in California and more than 400 in Washington state whom it suspects are non-citizens. The US Supreme Court rejected the California request, handing the Trump administration a snub a day before election day. Washington state has also refused the demand. Studies have repeatedly found non-citizen voting to be exceptionally rare. The Justice Department has warned election officials in every state that they could face prosecution if they knowingly allow non-citizens to vote. And Trump has offered $1 million for information leading to a voter fraud conviction, without giving details. At polling stations The Justice Department plans to send around 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states — its largest deployment ever. Monitoring is a decades-old practice, but Democrats and voting rights groups fear monitors could intimidate voters. The department says they will be unarmed, barred from interfering with voting and drawn from neither the FBI nor Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The administration says it is not planning operations targeting polling places, although Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said ICE agents could serve warrants there. Trump has declined to rule out declaring a national emergency or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows the president to deploy troops at home. A Civil War-era law bars troops and armed federal agents from polling places, and legal experts say an emergency declaration would not give the president power over elections. Counting the votes Federal agents could seek warrants or subpoenas for ballots, voting machines or records — potentially disrupting the count. In January, the FBI seized ballots and other 2020 election records in Fulton County, Georgia, a focus of Trump’s false claims that he won that year. Election officials warn that similar action during an active count could undermine safeguards tracking how ballots are handled. Trump could allege fraud involving mail-in ballots, voting machines or votes counted after election night, fueling demands for recounts or attempts to halt counting. But the US Supreme Court ruled in June that states may count mail ballots postmarked by election day that arrive afterward, and courts can intervene against unlawful disruption. After election day The Justice Department has sued Alaska to delay certification of its Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, citing a second candidate named Dan Sullivan who it says is trying to confuse voters, which he denies. Trump said he ordered the lawsuit. Experts say federal law does not allow the department to block certification, which courts can compel officials to carry out. Trump could pressure state officials to dispute results, as he did after losing the 2020 election. Experts warn unresolved disputes could also delay the seating of newly elected lawmakers in January. But courts have repeatedly upheld states’ authority over elections, and Democrats and voting rights groups have assembled legal teams to fight any interference. items.title: RDC : le représentant spécial du secrétaire général de l’ONU effectue une première rencontre avec Joseph Kabila à Goma
items.description: Le representant special du secretaire general de l'ONU et chef de la Mission de l'Organisation des Nations unies pour la stabilisation en Republique democratique du Congo (MONUSCO) James Swan est arrive le 2 novembre a Goma, au Nord-Kivu, a annonce la mission onusienne dans une publication sur X. Il y a rencontre le 3 novembre le chef du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), l'ancien president congolais Joseph Kabila. Sa visite s'inscrit dans le cadre de « consultations regulieres dans l'est de la RDC », a indique la MONUSCO. La rencontre est la premiere du genre depuis que l'ancien chef de l'etat a pris la tete du FRN, le 12 octobre. Le mouvement politico-militaire a succede a l'Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) et au Mouvement du 23 mars (M23). Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur de l'AFC, en est devenu l'un des vice-presidents, selon la presse congolaise. Pour la MONUSCO, il s'agit de poursuivre le dialogue que la mission avait noue avec l'AFC/M23. « Ces echanges visent a soutenir la mise en œuvre du mandat de la Mission », souligne-t-elle. Le representant special etait accompagne d'une delegation comprenant le general de brigade Givenz Kishombe Sichali, le conseiller principal Walter Lotze et le chef de bureau de l'adjoint du representant special charge de la protection et des operations Marilyn Ngum Fru. Pour sa part, le chef du mouvement etait seconde par Corneille Nangaa et Bertrand Bisimwa, deux vice-presidents, ainsi que par plusieurs collaborateurs, dont le colonel Imani Nzenze et Moïse Nyarugabo. Le FRN affirme vouloir honorer les engagements de Doha et s'opposer au renouvellement du mandat de la MONUSCO a l'issue des echanges, l'un des deux vice-presidents presents, Bertrand Bisimwa, a rendu compte de la position du mouvement. Selon lui, le FRN entend honorer les engagements pris lors des negociations de Doha, au Qatar, entre la delegation du gouvernement congolais et celle de l'ex-AFC/M23, dont il a herite « de l'actif et du passif ». Il a accuse les forces gouvernementales et leurs allies de reprendre les attaques sur plusieurs fronts. Selon le meme compte rendu, le FRN s'oppose au renouvellement du mandat de la MONUSCO et souhaite qu'elle poursuive son retrait de l'est de la RDC. Le meme dirigeant a qualifie le bilan de la MONUSCO d'« echec tota », mais a tout de meme reconnu qu'elle avait apporte un appui logistique aux dispositifs issus des discussions de Doha. Le FRN a aussi conteste un eventuel redeploiement de la mission au Sud-Kivu pour soutenir le mecanisme de verification du cessez-le-feu, a precise le responsable, pour qui son mouvement ne voit pas l'utilite de la presence de la MONUSCO dans les zones deja controlees par le FRN, presentees comme « stabilisees ». Le cessez-le-feu et la protection des civils au centre des discussions La MONUSCO a rappele que les consultations font partie de son mandat, qui consiste a proteger les civils, a faciliter l'acces humanitaire et a appuyer les mecanismes de suivi et de verification du cessez-le-feu dans l'est de la RDC. Parmi les dispositifs concernes figure le Mecanisme conjoint de verification elargi Plus (MCVE+), mis en place pour surveiller le respect de la treve entre le gouvernement congolais et l'AFC/M23. La MONUSCO contribue a la verification des violations presumees du cessez-le-feu et au suivi de son application sur le terrain.

items.title: Connecting Africa’s wallets, unlocking Africa’s trade, smartly
items.description: Yesterday, Monday, 2 November, I joined discussions at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra, including a Smart Africa Steering Committee roundtable. My main message was that connecting Africa’s mobile money wallets across borders, alongside visa-free travel, could transform intra-African trade, significantly. At the Africa Prosperity Network (APN), we estimate that implementing both reforms could help raise intra-African trade from around 16% to more than 25% within five years. The opportunity is enormous. The figures I presented show that US$2.1 trillion flowed through mobile money wallets globally in 2025, with approximately US$1.4 trillion, two-thirds of the total, transacted in sub-Saharan Africa. Africa had some 1.2 billion registered accounts, while West Africa alone recorded approximately US$498 billion in transactions across 517 million accounts. These are accounts, rather than unique individuals. Yet our commercial strength remains constrained by fragmented markets, compared with intra-regional trade figures of approximately 59% in Asia and 68% in Europe. Fragmentation also makes payments expensive. It is estimated that more than 80% of payments between African countries pass through banks outside the continent, with associated payment and currency-conversion arrangements costing Africa approximately US$5.3 billion annually. Within states, we have built mobile money at extraordinary scale. Take Ghana, for instance, which was the first to do comprehensive mobile money interoperability, last August alone, over one billion mobile money transactions were recorded in one single month. We must now connect those wallets and put them to work for continental trade, for greater opportunities and jobs. Imagine a trader in Kumasi buying from a supplier in Abidjan: she pays in cedis from her wallet, and the supplier receives CFA francs quickly, securely and affordably. Neither needs to source dollars or carry cash across a border. Multiply that transaction across millions of businesses. Lower costs will release money for stock and expansion. Faster settlement will improve cash flow. Reliable transaction records can also support access to credit and insurance. For women, SMEs and young entrepreneurs, this could place Africa’s single market directly in their hands. But a trader who can pay a supplier must also be able to travel to inspect goods, negotiate and build trust, if need be. Free movement and seamless payments should, therefore, go hand in hand. Since the inaugural Africa Prosperity Dialogues in 2023, APN has brought together policymakers, the AfCFTA Secretariat, Smart Africa, GSMA Africa, telecommunications companies and financial institutions to advance this agenda. The 2024 Peduase Action Compact helped sustain that momentum. At the Sixth AU Mid-Year Coordination Meeting in Accra that July, leaders committed to working towards wider PAPSS participation, cross-border mobile money interoperability, connected payment channels, common regulatory safeguards and stronger digital infrastructure by 2027. This is what makes the timing and focus of APD 2027 significant. Trusted identity is essential to delivering these ambitions. This is why APN supports the Smart Africa Trust Alliance (SATA) and Smart Africa Data Exchange (SADX). SATA establishes the framework for cooperation; SADX enables national systems to securely verify and exchange information while countries retain control over their data. Nineteen countries have signed the SATA Declaration. Ghana, Benin and Rwanda have completed the first phase of the SADX pilot, demonstrating cross-border identity verification in a controlled testing environment. We believe this can help address a major obstacle to visa-free travel: governments’ uncertainty about visitors’ identities. Allowing authorised agencies to verify travellers against official records in their home countries, with privacy and security safeguards, could strengthen border management and greatly reduce those concerns. Trusted digital identity can also support access to financial services across borders. We are hopeful because progress is visible. Since our Make Africa Borderless Now! campaign began this year, several countries have introduced or announced visa-free policies for Africans. These sovereign decisions demonstrate growing political willingness to open our borders. Expanding participation in PAPSS and the 19 SATA signatories are equally encouraging. The foundations for freer movement, trusted identities and seamless payments are coming together. With sustained political leadership, regulatory cooperation and industry action, we can achieve significant progress towards continent-wide mobile money interoperability by the end of 2027. A system that allows authorised agencies to verify a visitor’s identity against official records in their home country, with appropriate privacy and security safeguards, could greatly reduce the uncertainty that fuels resistance to visa-free travel. Governments would have greater confidence about who is entering their countries, while traders and other travellers could face fewer delays and obstacles. We believe this can strengthen the political case for opening borders and, over time, support the identity checks needed to access financial services across countries. Connecting Africa’s identities, alongside its wallets, can help build the confidence needed to let our people move freely and trade more. This is the agenda for the Africa Prosperity Dialogues, taking place in Accra from 13–15 January 2027: “The Africa We Want Is Borderless. Move Freely. Pay Seamlessly. Trade More.” When Africans move, their money and businesses should move with them. For us at APN, free movement and seamless payments go hand in hand, and trusted digital identity can help connect the two. Join us to help make all this possible by registering: www.apd2027.africaprosperitynetwork.com The author is the Foundet and Executive Chairman of APN. He can be reached on gabby@africaprosperity.network

items.title: Imran's nephew denied jail meeting this time; PTI open to possible alliance with JUI-F
items.description: ISLAMABAD: PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was again denied a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday – a prescribed day by the Islamabad High Court for meetings at the Adiala jail. The denial comes just a day after Imran’s lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet him and his incarcerated wife Bushra Bibi for consultations on a legal case. The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months. Speaking to Dawn on Tuesday, Advocate Awais Younas Chaudhry said a son of Imran’s sister Uzma Khanum, Abdullah Khan, reached Adiala jail as a family member to meet the PTI founder. However, authorities did not grant him permission, said Chaudhry, who had submitted a list of lawyers and party leaders to the Adiala jail administration for meetings with Imran. Chaudhry, whose name was also included in the list, said that lawyers, including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, also reached the prison, but were not allowed to meet the ex-premier. Imran’s sisters — Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan — used to stage frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release. However, the three sisters have remained detained since late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad. Potential JUI-F support Meanwhile, PTI has hinted that it can get support from Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in the struggle against the government. Speaking to the media, the PTI secretary general remarked that no one was terming Fazl a “saviour”, but the PTI would welcome everyone who would stand by the party and struggle against the incumbent government. “It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” Raja said. “We do not depend on anyone, and we do not have expectations from anyone,” Raja stated. However, he emphasised that the party wanted its caravan to grow, hinting towards a possible PTI–JUI-F alliance if Fazl offers to join. Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments. Since mid-October , the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights. Gohar refutes rumour that Imran ‘happy’ about KP governor’s rule Separately, the PTI chairman dismissed the notion that Imran himself wanted his party’s government in KP to be sacked and was happy with the imposition of governor’s rule . “It is not correct,” Barrister Gohar said. Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar informed him, after his meeting with Imran, that the jailed ex-premier was already aware of the measures and he did not say that it was a positive step as they did not talk much about politics. The federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder. Replying to a question, Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar did not bring any political message from jail. Nevertheless, the PTI chairman welcomed Monday’s meeting with Imran as a positive development. He hoped that the political tension would end, rejecting the reports of any forward bloc in PTI’s KP wing. Last month, there were rumours of a group of KP MPAs endorsing Ali Amin Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar. However, PTI soon clarified that Akbar remained the party’s president for KP and named Senator Noorul Haq Qadri to take over his duties in his absence. Similarly, after several PTI parliamentarians questioned the party’s decisions and overreliance on Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is non-functional during governor’s rule — PTI reaffirmed its support for him. In its latest clarification a day ago, PTI insisted there was no “factionalism” or “division” within the party, and warned of action against any member who violates party discipline or policy.

items.title: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the leadership of the Department of State Services, DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally. Atiku said the alleged plot was part of a broader attempt by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to frustrate opposition parties, undermine political competition and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose their leaders ahead of the 2027 general election. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, the former vice president alleged that public facilities meant for campaign activities had been blocked and logistical support withheld in Sokoto, describing the developments as deliberate efforts to deny the ADC a level playing field. He said information available to the party indicated that protesters were being mobilised from an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road, with trucks deployed to strategic locations, including a roundabout. According to him, the protesters were causing gridlock, threatening commuters and beating some residents, while some had moved away from the roundabout to find shade. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform,” Atiku said. “Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis.” He called on security officers allegedly involved in the mobilisation to stop immediately and return to their constitutional duty of impartial service. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of devoting much of its energy over the past three and a half years to weakening credible opposition, alleging that its strategy of absorbing former opposition figures into the APC was aimed at reducing Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name. The former vice president also linked the alleged obstruction of the rally to the economic hardship facing Nigerians, saying the government should be defending its record on the rising cost of food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials rather than trying to stop opposition campaigns. “Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive,” he said. “That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.” Atiku pledged that an ADC government would make life affordable through policies to support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. He said the party would also pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, aimed at providing measurable relief to consumers while strengthening domestic industry. The ADC presidential candidate accused the APC of resorting to intimidation and obstruction after what he described as the failure of its last rally in Kaduna, saying the party should have taken the outcome as a warning that Nigerians were withdrawing their confidence. These are the last kicks of a dying horse,” Atiku said. “The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence.” Atiku said the 2027 general election would be a defining moment in Nigeria’s democratic history, insisting that the contest was not merely between political parties or candidates but between a government he accused of indifference to citizens’ suffering and Nigerians determined to make their votes count. He vowed that the ADC would resist what he described as administrative roadblocks and underhand manoeuvres designed to exclude the opposition, adding that he would be in Sokoto on Wednesday to address residents. “I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state,” he said. He urged residents to remain peaceful and avoid being provoked into violence, while calling on security agencies to protect commuters, residents and rally participants without favour. Atiku also warned that officers who colluded in suppressing political freedom would be held accountable under the law, while pledging support for those who refused to be used against democracy. He urged Nigerians to remain resolute in defending their democratic rights, declaring that the country belonged to its people and not any political party or temporary occupant of power. items.title: Deaths linked to Hamile explosion rise to three, 10 others injured
items.description: The death toll from Tuesday’s explosion involving a tricycle reportedly transporting suspected dynamite at Hamile in the Upper West Region has risen to three, including a Ghanaian Immigration Service (GIS) officer. JoyNews’ Upper West Regional Correspondent, Rafiq Salam, reports that two civilians have died following the incident, bringing the total number of fatalities to three. Ten other people have also sustained injuries and are receiving medical treatment. The explosion occurred on Tuesday, November 3, after security personnel reportedly pursued a tricycle carrying suspected explosive materials along an unauthorised route. Preliminary information suggests that the occupants of the tricycle failed to stop when they encountered security personnel at a checkpoint, leading to a pursuit that ended in the explosion. An immigration officer was killed in the incident, while another officer sustained critical injuries. The explosion has heightened tensions in the border community, with residents reportedly gathering at the Ghana Immigration Service checkpoint to demand the withdrawal of immigration personnel. JoyNews’ Rafiq Salam also reports that military personnel have been deployed to the area following the incident. He reports that the two fatalities were the result of stray bullets from the military personnel, but the immigration officer was killed by the explosion. Meanwhile, the government has imposed an 11-hour curfew on Hamile Township and its surrounding communities in the Lambussie District of the Upper West Region following the incident. items.title: 2027: DLA suspends Adebisi’s presidential campaign, refers him to EFCC, police
items.description: …distances itself from candidate, warns members against promoting his candidature By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA) has suspended all presidential campaign activities by its 2027 candidate, Moses Adebisi, pending the outcome of disciplinary proceedings against him and ongoing criminal investigations by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the police. The party said it had withdrawn institutional backing from Adebisi’s campaign over concerns arising from a personal financial undertaking allegedly made before his emergence as its presidential candidate, including a dud cheque, while reserving the right to take further political decisions on its participation in the presidential election. The position was contained in a statement by the party’s National Chairman and Leader, Barr. Samuel Memeh, who said the DLA had initiated disciplinary proceedings against Adebisi and referred the matter to the EFCC and the Inspector-General of Police for independent investigation. According to the statement, the party’s National Disciplinary Committee invited Adebisi to appear before it on August 30, 2026, following a letter dated August 29. “Following that proceeding, the Committee issued a directive suspending all presidential campaign activities and public appearances relating to his candidature pending further resolution,” Memeh said. The party said it would not assume responsibility for personal financial undertakings or transactions entered into by any individual without its authorisation, stressing that Adebisi remained personally responsible for his commitments. It also distanced itself from his personal activities and political engagements that were not expressly authorised by the party, warning the public against treating his representations as official DLA commitments. The party reaffirmed that all presidential campaign activities and public projection relating to Adebisi’s candidature remained suspended until further notice. It said further decisions would be taken after the disciplinary committee submitted its recommendations, adding that it reserved the right to determine its political participation in the 2027 presidential election. The DLA also directed its candidates and campaign organisations to stop promoting Adebisi as its presidential candidate while the suspension remained in force. “All campaigns and public political activities undertaken by our candidates shall be regulated, coordinated, and supervised by the National Campaign Council, under the authority of the National Working Committee and the National Leadership,” Memeh said. The party warned that candidates who displayed Adebisi’s photographs in campaign posters, flyers, banners, billboards or digital materials in ways suggesting official endorsement could face disciplinary action. It, however, urged Nigerians to support its candidates contesting governorship, National Assembly, state Houses of Assembly and other elective positions in the 2027 elections. The DLA said its candidates were selected through established party processes, with emphasis on character, competence, leadership capacity and commitment to public service. It said they would prioritise security, education, healthcare, agriculture, technological advancement, employment creation and institutional accountability. On the state of the nation, the party called on President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government to account transparently for public revenue and expenditure, insisting that Nigerians deserved to know how government policies were affecting their welfare. It also urged the government to recruit more security personnel, rebuild damaged security formations and establish additional security units in vulnerable communities, particularly rural and farming settlements. “Security must reach every community. Farmers must be able to access their farmlands safely, businesses must operate without fear, and citizens must be protected wherever they live,” the party said. The DLA also criticised state governors for what it described as insufficient innovation and strategic leadership in addressing the challenges confronting their people, urging them to deliver measurable results in security, agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic development. The party called for a shift from excessive consumption and import dependence towards production, manufacturing, science, technology, agriculture and renewable energy, saying Nigeria needed leadership founded on integrity, competence, innovation and accountability. The DLA urged its members to remain united and disciplined, insisting that no individual was greater than the institution. With its disciplinary process still pending, the party said it would communicate further decisions after considering the committee’s recommendations, leaving open the possibility of fresh political and constitutional action over its presidential candidature.
