items.title: Halal : 80% des viandes de cet abattoir espagnol est destinée à l’Algérie
items.description: Alors que la cinquième version du cahier des charges de la certification halal de la Grande Mosquée de Paris entre en vigueur le 1er janvier 2027, Chems-Eddine Hafiz, recteur de la plus importante institution musulmans de France, a reçu les responsables d’abattoirs européens. Mais si l’Espagne reste le pays qui approvisionne le plus l’Algérie en viande halal, selon le recteur. Selon Cosme Javaloyes, directeur de l’abattoir espagnol Matadero Orihuela, « 80% de sa production est destinée au marché algérien ». « Nous abattons 3 500 veaux et 30 000 agneaux par mois » « Nous abattons 3500 veaux et 30 000 agneaux par mois. 80% de la production est destinée au marché algérien. Nous expédions la viande depuis Alicante, Valence et Alméria vers les ports d’Oran, Mostaganem et Ghazaouet », a précisé le patron de cet abattoir basé dans la région d’Alicante dans le sud de l’Espagne dans un entretien à la web TV de la Grande mosquée de Paris. À la Grande Mosquée de Paris, le recteur Chems-eddine Hafiz a réuni des responsables d’abattoirs venus de plusieurs pays européens, notamment d’Espagne, d’Italie, de Pologne et de Roumanie. Une rencontre placée sous le signe du dialogue et de l’exigence, à l’approche de l’entrée… pic.twitter.com/LHIxdZjN25 — Grande Mosquée de Paris (@mosqueedeparis) November 1, 2026 Pour M. Javaolyes, la certification halal de la Grande Mosquée de Paris constitue une « garantie de qualité » et de « conformité religieuse, essentielle au développement des relations commerciales et à la confiance des consommateurs. » Certification Halal : la Grande mosquée de Paris attire de nouveaux marchés Lors de cette rencontre, le recteur de la Grande mosquée de Paris a affirmé sa volonté de renforcer ses relations avec les directeurs d’abattoirs venus également, principalement, d’Italie, d’Espagne, de Pologne et de Roumanie. 70 % de la production de l'abattoir espagnol Matadero Orihuela est destinée au marché algérien. Invité à la Grande Mosquée de Paris dans le cadre de la rencontre européenne des responsables d'abattoirs, Cosme Javaloyes, directeur de Matadero Orihuela, installé dans la région… pic.twitter.com/cuAEeOwz4o — Grande Mosquée de Paris (@mosqueedeparis) November 1, 2026 Lors de sa prise de parole, le recteur a affirmé à ses partenaires sa volonté de renforcer les exigences du cahier des charges afin de « garantir la rigueur, la conformité et la fiabilité de la certification halal au service des consommateurs musulmans ». Pour cela, M. Hafiz compte sur des imams et des érudits religieux de la mosquée afin de rendre ce cahier des charges le plus conforme possible aux exigences religieuses. Ce cahier des charges a pour objectif « d’éclairer les consommateurs musulmans des normes applicables, dans une jurisprudence constante qui s’enrichit des données juridiques nouvelles en matière de biotechnologies, afin de qualifier le caractère licite ou illicite des consommables mis au point par l’industrie agroalimentaire », selon le site officiel de la Grande Mosquée de Paris. L’enjeu est donc, pour les professionnels du secteur qui travaillent en collaboration avec la Grande Mosquée de Paris, d’allier les exigences liées aux règles religieuses du halal à la réglementation européenne en vigueur en matière d’abattage. Par cette volonté d’actualiser le cahier des charges de façon à le rendre plus exigeant et strictement conforme aux règles de licéité halal, et de renforcer ses relations avec de multiples abattoirs européens, le recteur a marqué sa volonté de viser de nouveaux marchés. En effet, un cahier des charges exigeant, c’est d’autant plus de consommateurs qui, ayant confiance en la certification de la Grande Mosquée de Paris, vont se fournir en cette viande. Le recteur réitère par ailleurs l’importance de la certification grande mosquée de Paris, auprès de ces entreprises, en ce que, depuis 2022, le gouvernement algérien impose que toute viande importée l’ait reçu pour entrer sur son sol. L’article Halal : 80% des viandes de cet abattoir espagnol est destinée à l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Fresh oil spill disrupts fishing in Bayelsa community
items.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A fresh crude oil spill has polluted the shoreline of Egweama community on Cape Formosa Island in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, disrupting fishing activities and leaving residents stranded. The incident, which occurred on Sunday, November 1, 2026, was documented in a field report by the Environmental Conservation Agriculture and Rural Development (ECARD). The organisation said the spill was reported to it the following day, with its Chief Operating Officer, Alagoa Morris, subsequently conducting a follow-up assessment. According to the report, crude oil had spread across the water surface along the Atlantic coastline, affecting the livelihood of residents who depend mainly on fishing. It said jerrycans, drums and plastic basins were seen filled with crude oil, while some youths were observed scooping the pollutant into containers on Monday morning. A resident, Ms Ebimiete David, said community members had spent several hours collecting crude oil from the shoreline. She said children first reported seeing crude oil along the shoreline between 5pm and 6pm on Sunday, adding that the volume increased when the tide came in around 8pm. David said residents continued scooping the oil into containers until about 3am, when the water receded and carried away a large quantity of the pollutant. Also recounting the impact of the spill, Chief Souyo Amasara-Inengite, described as the first settler at one of the fishing camps along the affected shoreline, said the incident had prevented fishermen from going to sea. He said the oil covered the water surface when they attempted to go fishing between 7pm and 8pm on Sunday, adding that some fishing nets had also been contaminated and damaged. “We are all stranded on land now. Just now I went out to the sea to drop my fishing nets but there was no way; everywhere is crude oil and I returned disappointed,” he said. Confirming the incident, Chairman of the Community Development Committee (CDC), Mr Tonye Yemoleigha, called for urgent intervention and cleanup. In a statement titled, “Oil spill: Egweama community cries out for immediate help, Cleanup,” Yemoleigha said the community was uncertain about the source of the spill. He, however, said unconfirmed reports from community sources suggested that it might have originated from the activities of Aiteo Oil Company, whose vessels transport crude from Nembe Creek to the Atlantic. Yemoleigha urged the Bayelsa State Government to intervene and ensure that the responsible oil company undertook immediate remedial action and cleanup. He also called for medical and relief materials to cushion the socioeconomic impact of the incident on affected residents. ECARD described the incident as another example of the recurring problem of “mystery spills”, in which the source of oil pollution remains unidentified and operating companies deny responsibility. The organisation cited previous offshore incidents, including the 2024 Foropa community spill and the 2021 Sangana/Koluama incident, where Conoil was suspected but the results of investigations were not made public. It said crude oil fingerprint analysis could help identify the source of such spills by comparing samples collected from affected sites with crude from suspected facilities. “The only way to solve the mystery of a mystery spill is resorting to ‘fingerprint analysis’ of the crude oil samples from the impacted sites which could reveal the operator whose facility actually discharged crude oil into the environment,” the report stated. ECARD called on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA), the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) and the Bayelsa State Ministry of Environment to investigate the incident, establish its source and ensure immediate cleanup. It also advocated better funding and equipment for regulatory agencies, independent environmental monitoring, prompt response to spills and stronger collaboration with the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) and the Nigerian Navy to address recurring offshore pollution. The organisation said no individual or company should be allowed to pollute the environment and deny residents their rights to health and livelihood. “Nobody or corporation has the right to pollute the environment and deny others their right to life, health and livelihood. Denying fisher folks their means of livelihood is unacceptable,” it stated. The post Fresh oil spill disrupts fishing in Bayelsa community appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kebbi set to implement ₦70,000 transportation allowance for workers
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Kebbi State Government has said it is ready to implement a ₦70,000 transport allowance for workers in the state to cushion the high transport fares occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy. The State Governor, Comrade Nasir Idris, disclosed this on Tuesday during an interview with journalists in Abuja. Recall that the Kebbi State Government approved a ₦75,000 minimum wage for state workers and an additional ₦17,650 for teachers. Asked whether the state would pay workers the ₦70,000 recently approved for federal workers, to be implemented from November, Governor Idris said he had already set up a committee for the implementation of the transport allowance. He expressed concern over the declining purchasing power of the current minimum wage due to economic hardship, adding that a committee under the Head of Service was currently working on a further adjustment. “I just came back from a journey, and, by God’s grace, I know what the Federal Government has decided to do for workers. You should also know that, being a labour leader, something must definitely be done for Kebbi State workers. “I have already set up a committee under the Head of Service, and they are working. I have said, time without number, that if the Federal Government increases workers’ salaries, Kebbi State will be among the first states to implement it. “The President has done well by approving the ₦70,000 transport intervention. The President believes that the purchasing power of the existing ₦70,000 national minimum wage has been affected by the economic situation. That is why he graciously approved the ₦70,000 transport allowance before the new minimum wage will be negotiated.” The Governor emphasised his commitment to maintaining industrial harmony by prioritising the needs of workers and artisans. To ensure conducive working conditions, the Comrade Governor said his administration had embarked on the development of workers’ housing projects, including a project for 155 houses and another for 250 units, some of which are expected to be commissioned by December. He also absorbed over 1,700 casual workers he inherited into full-time employment to ensure job security, while an additional 2,000 teachers and various health workers, including doctors, nurses, and pharmacists, have been recruited under his leadership. Governor Idris highlighted his efforts to foster better synergy and cooperation between workers and the government. On revenue generation and fiscal management, the former labour leader said significant improvements had been made in internally generated revenue by closing leakages. He asserted that revenue collection had increased significantly compared with previous administrations. The Governor said his administration does not owe workers’ salaries, pensions, gratuities, or other benefits, attributing the successful financial management to the prudent use of resources despite increased responsibilities. He noted that while allocations had tripled, the associated administrative burdens and challenges had also increased significantly. On infrastructure, Governor Idris said major road projects were being facilitated through cooperation with President Bola Tinubu’s administration, stressing that completed road works had significantly reduced travel times. He defended President Tinubu’s current policies against claims that they were causing hardship, noting that they were necessary for long-term stability. He encouraged citizens to endure the current economic challenges so that future generations may benefit from a better economy. The post Kebbi set to implement ₦70,000 transportation allowance for workers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
items.description: Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House. Multiple polls predict Democrats will take control of the House of Representatives and have a shot at seizing the Senate on the back of voter resentment at a deeply unpopular president, soaring energy costs and the dragging conflict with Iran. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. Voters cast their ballots inside a polling location in the social hall at St Patrick’s Church on November 3, 2026 in Youngstown, Ohio. — AFP Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in an Atlanta suburb, told AFP he “voted for mostly Democratic candidates”. “It’s just about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things,” Comer said. “It needs to change for the everyday person and I’m an everyday person.” Trump defended his record in a final TV phone-in pitch to voters on Tuesday, saying he had rebuilt the country through his immigration crackdown, war on Iran and tariff policy. “We have to keep America great. We’re great now. We were terrible two years ago,” Trump told “Fox & Friends”. The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands. Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans. A person holds a sticker, during the US midterm elections, in Durham, North Carolina, US, November 3. — Reuters The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s. In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff, who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future. “I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP . Economic discontent Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals. But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool. Democratic US Senate candidate Chris Pappas speaks to members of the media after voting in the US midterm elections at Webster Elementary School in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, November 3. — Reuters “This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.” Some Republican supporters remain confident. “We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP . But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority. Disputed results? More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating high engagement. A voter poses with their “I Voted” sticker after submitting their ballot at a polling place in the Marine on St Croix City Hall on November 3, 2026 in Marine on St Croix, Minnesota. — AFP The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts. As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans. Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating. The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election. And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens. Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats. “I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

items.title: Things Are Going to Get Ugly
items.description: Donald Trump won’t be able to cope. If he loses control of one chamber of Congress, never mind both, the world will see a personality collapse and rage meltdown on the scale of the final sequence of the Lord of the Rings . The Donald Trump of 2018 could cope, barely. Back then, he had a number of things going for him. First, although Republicans suffered heavy losses in the House, they gained two seats in the Senate. Trump interpreted the Senate gains as proof that “people like me,” and the House losses as a rebuke to Trump-disloyal Republicans. “Mia Love,” he said of a Republican who lost her seat in Utah, “gave me no love, but then she lost. Too bad.” Second, the Trump of 2018 had the benefit of a strong economy. The war he was fighting in Iraq and Syria was going well and commanded broad bipartisan support, given that it had started under President Obama. Third, Trump did not have a lot personally at stake in the election of 2018. The big threat to him that year was the investigation of his Russia connections by Special Counsel Robert Mueller. The Mueller investigation was conducted within the executive branch. That investigation had been initiated even though the Republicans held the House, and Trump was later able to contain the damage from the investigation even though Republicans lost the House. Fourth, Trump in 2018 was younger, nimbler, and planning for the future: his reelection race in 2020. Polls sometimes miss. But if the most recent ones are accurate, the Trump of 2026 faces big losses in both chambers, all of them directly implicating him. The president opened a Senate seat in North Carolina by harrying the incumbent Republican, Thom Tillis, into retirement. Former Governor Roy Cooper, a Democrat, now appears headed to a victory so big that he may flip the state legislature too, potentially upending one of the most successful Republican congressional gerrymanders. In the race for Ohio governor, Trump endorsed Vivek Ramaswamy, whose noxious campaign may cost the GOP not only another Senate seat, but the state legislature too. Trump even put a Senate seat in Texas in play by favoring the radioactive Ken Paxton over the popular incumbent, John Cornyn. Trump also started a war with Iran that he is not winning. He imposed tariffs that have raised prices and hurt farmers. He accelerated inflation with the deficits exacerbated by his so-called big beautiful bill. [ ead: Trump is closing from behind ] The Trump of 2026 has a lot at stake in today’s unignorable election. The second Trump administration is a network of scandals and corruption. Subpoena power in the hands of his opponents will expose Trump and his family to enormous legal and political risk. Unlike in 2018, large numbers of Americans connect Trump’s self-enrichment to their economic decline. Gallup found that 89 percent of Americans agree that corruption is widespread in government, up 10 points from just a year ago, and up 30 points from 20 years ago. That’s far higher than in any other developed country, comparable to levels found in Lebanon, Peru, Ghana and Nigeria. The Trump of 2026 is more addled and more clumsy than the Trump of 2018. In his final pre-election speech, he reminded voters of his botched renovation of the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall in Washington, D.C.—and mused about renaming the pool after himself. Trump’s style of politics is authoritarian. He does not inspire or negotiate. He issues orders. He demands submission. He makes everything about himself. Trump never tried to broaden his support. He blatantly favored disaster-aid requests from states with Republican governors over those from states with Democratic governors. He was more likely to apportion tariff relief to firms that donated to Republicans, and more likely to refuse relief to firms that did not. When he encountered opposition in Congress, he responded with insults that permanently alienated legislators whose help he might need later. [ Peter Wehner: The MAGA reckoning arrives ] Trump ruled his party by fear, and now the fear is ebbing. On Sunday, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis made a campaign appearance near Mar-a-Lago to call on Republicans to take concerns about rising gas prices seriously—a cost most Americans blame on Trump’s Iran war. On November 1, the commentator Tucker Carlson posted on X a claim that Trump was planning a nuclear strike on Iran—and that only Vice President Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff stood in his way. Somebody who supports Vance is leaking to enhance his appeal at the expense of the president. Trump will not respond patiently to such challenges from within. He holds hundreds of millions of dollars in his MAGA Super PAC and related entities. Whatever remains after the races this year could then go toward sustaining the Trump family’s political power—conceivably backing a future presidential bid by one of Trump’s children. If the Democrats take the House and subpoenas start arriving, Trump will still retain control of the U.S. military and U.S. security services. He can indict people, he can invade nations, he can invoke emergency powers. He will get angrier, noisier, and crazier. He doesn’t care about the future of his party. He doesn’t care about the future of the country. He will want to punish a nation that, in his view, has ungratefully rejected him. Corruptly obtained money never feels secure. Trump, his children, and his inner group of close friends and sycophants most enriched in the past two years have a lot to worry about as the minutes of Trump’s presidency tick down. The worst is yet to come.

items.title: Tinubu’s Rivers rally to spotlight appointments, projects
items.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — Federal appointments secured by Rivers indigenes and infrastructure projects executed by the Federal Government are expected to feature prominently at the campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu in Port Harcourt on Saturday, November 7. The rally, scheduled to hold at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, is expected to attract political leaders, All Progressives Congress (APC) members and supporters from across Rivers State. A chieftain of the APC in the state, Barrister Princewill Dike, said the event would provide an opportunity to highlight the appointments and development projects credited to the Tinubu administration in Rivers. Dike, a member of the Publicity and Media Committee of the Tinubu Campaign Organisation in the state, listed several federal appointments secured by Rivers indigenes. They include Ambassador Desmond Akawor, Federal Commissioner representing Rivers State on the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), whose appointment was approved by Tinubu in November 2023 and subsequently confirmed by the Senate. He also mentioned Boma Iyaye, Executive Director, Finance and Administration of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), and Chief Tony Okocha, who represents Rivers State on the commission’s governing board. Other appointees listed by Dike are Senator Magnus Abe, Chairman of the National Agency for the Great Green Wall, and Chief Victor Tombari Giadom, Chairman of the Nigerian Institute of Educational Planning and Administration. Dike also cited a disclosure reportedly made by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, on October 24, 2026, that Rivers State had secured at least 49 federal appointments under the Tinubu administration. The appointments, according to the reported disclosure, include directors-general, executive secretaries and heads of federal agencies. On infrastructure, Dike highlighted the 37.9-kilometre Bodo-Bonny Road, which was temporarily opened in December 2025, providing a direct road connection between Bonny Island and the mainland. He said the road had reduced the island’s long-standing dependence on river transportation and helicopter services. He also listed sections of the East-West Road, particularly the Eleme Junction-Port Harcourt-Ahoada and Eleme Junction-Onne Port corridors, among the Federal Government’s infrastructure interventions in the Niger Delta. Other projects cited include the 700-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which traverses nine states, including Rivers, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom and Cross River. Dike further mentioned NDDC projects such as the Kaa-Ataba Bridge, linking Khana and Andoni Local Government Areas, and the Bonny Ring Road and Bridges being undertaken in collaboration with the Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG). He also listed the Federal University of Environment and Technology (FUET), located at Koroma/Saakpenwa in Tai Local Government Area of Ogoniland. According to him, the November 7 rally would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to discuss federal representation, infrastructure development and the future of Rivers State. He said the event would also enable the state’s political leaders to express appreciation to Tinubu for what he described as his goodwill towards Rivers and assure him of the state’s support in the 2027 elections. The post Tinubu’s Rivers rally to spotlight appointments, projects appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Affaire City Club : les peines maximales requises contre Jonathan Harroch
items.description: Le procureur général du Roi près la cour d'appel de Casablanca a requis, mardi 3 novembre, la condamnation de Stéphane Jonathan Harroch, propriétaire du groupe de salles de sport « City Club », pour le crime de traite des êtres humains, réclamant l’application des peines les plus sévères prévues par la loi. Lors de son réquisitoire prononcé en audience, le représentant du ministère public a affirmé que l'accusé profitait de la situation de ses employées pour les attirer et leur imposer des pratiques sexuelles déviantes, en plus de violences et d'humiliations répétées ayant également visé le personnel masculin. Insistant sur la spécificité de la qualification de traite des êtres humains, le magistrat a rappelé que cette infraction touche directement à la dignité et que le législateur retient sa constitution dès lors que l'intention coupable est établie. Il a par ailleurs souligné que l'affaire a éclaté grâce au courage d'une femme ayant brisé le silence sur les réseaux sociaux pour dénoncer les sévices et l'exploitation subis par les salariés du groupe. Évoquant le cas de la victime Ali, le substitut du procureur général a relaté les violences et la séquestration décrites par l'intéressé devant la chambre, précisant que ces faits sont corroborés par des enregistrements de caméras et les déclarations de témoins. Le représentant du parquet a fustigé les insultes et le mépris dont le chef d'entreprise abreuvait ses collaborateurs, en dépit de leur haut niveau d'instruction. Concernant la victime Ghizlane, recrutée sans contrat et privée de salaire après le premier mois de travail, le magistrat a rapporté des faits particulièrement graves : l'accusé aurait exigé d'elle une relation avec un entraîneur en vue de concevoir un enfant destiné à être cédé à l'étranger pour des réseaux pédophiles, ce qui a poussé la jeune femme à fuir son emploi. Il a également été fait état de harcèlement assorti de promesses de promotions, de rémunérations et d'un appartement, conditionnées à la participation à des soirées privées. Le réquisitoire s'est ensuite arrêté sur la situation des victimes Kaoutar et Soukaina, toutes deux appréhendées lors de la descente policière dans l'hôtel. Pour Kaoutar, en grande détresse matérielle, l’embauche a été conditionnée à des faveurs sexuelles, une somme de 15.000 dirhams lui avait été remise par le mis en cause à des fins d'exploitation sexuelle avant d'être saisie par les enquêteurs. Quant à Soukaina, retrouvée dévêtue aux côtés de l'accusé lors de l'intervention, elle a subi des relations sexuelles dictées par la précarité financière avant de faire l'objet de dénigrements, sa propre sœur ayant également été exploitée sexuellement par le gérant. Le magistrat a insisté sur le fait que la fragilité socio-économique de ces jeunes femmes a été délibérément instrumentalisée par l’employeur. Le prévenu est poursuivi pour incitation à la débauche et à la prostitution, harcèlement sexuel, traite des êtres humains, détention et usage illicite de stupéfiants, proxénétisme avec contrainte et menaces de diffamation par captation d'images, et d'attentat à la pudeur avec violences. items.title: 3 Nigerians arrested over robberies targeting bank customers in Kumasi
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has arrested three Nigerian nationals suspected of belonging to a criminal syndicate allegedly involved in a series of robberies targeting bank customers in Kumasi and its surrounding communities. In a statement signed by Superintendent of Police Godwin Ahianyo, Head of the Ashanti Regional Police Command’s Public Affairs Unit, the Command said the arrests followed an intelligence-led operation by an IGP’s Special Team on Saturday, 31 October 2026, to apprehend the suspected members of the group. The operation, according to the police, took place at about 11.30 p.m., and involved personnel from the Anti-Armed Robbery Unit of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Headquarters and the Accra Regional Police Intelligence Directorate (PID). Providing details of the exercise, the Police said the operation led to the arrest of two Nigerian nationals, Aboy Promise, 30, and Favour Uwalaka, 45, at a hotel in Moshie Zongo, Kumasi. A search of their rooms uncovered GH¢1,600 in cash, assorted mobile phones, a Royal motorbike and a master key suspected to have been used to gain unauthorised access to vehicles belonging to bank customers. The Command, detailing the items recovered during the operation, stated: “A search conducted in their rooms resulted in the recovery of GH¢1,600.00, assorted mobile phones, a Royal motorbike and a master key used to gain unauthorised access to victims’ vehicles and steal cash.” Investigations into the alleged activities of the suspects have pointed to a pattern of targeting individuals who withdraw substantial amounts of money from banks. According to the Police, the syndicate monitored banking premises, identified customers who made large withdrawals and followed them before attacking and robbing them. The Command explained that the group also allegedly broke into unattended vehicles belonging to bank customers, using a master key to access the cars and steal cash kept inside. During interrogation, the two arrested suspects reportedly admitted their involvement in the robberies and provided information about two other alleged accomplices. The Police disclosed that the suspects identified the individuals as Chinedu, alias Alhaji, and Kingsley, alias KC. Acting on the information obtained, the police team proceeded to another hotel at Dechemso, a suburb of Kumasi, where the third suspect, Kingsley, alias KC, aged 35, was arrested. He is also a Nigerian national. However, the fourth suspected member of the group, Chinedu, alias Alhaji, remains at large. Appealing for public assistance to locate him, the Ashanti Regional Police Command urged anyone with credible information about his whereabouts to report to the nearest police station. The Command stated: “The Command is appealing to the general public to volunteer any credible information that could lead to his arrest.” It further advised the public to contact the Police through emergency numbers 191 and 112 or the toll-free MTN and Telecel line 18555. The Police also disclosed that the three suspects had admitted to robbing a victim of GH¢15,000 at Asokore Mampong on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, after the individual withdrew the money from Kwamang Rural Bank. Providing further details of the alleged offences, the Command said the suspects had also admitted to similar robberies at the Atonsu branch of Fidelity Bank, the Ahodwo branch of Access Bank and other locations within Kumasi and its surrounding communities. The three arrested suspects have since been handed over to the Ashanti Regional Police Command and are assisting with ongoing investigations. Meanwhile, the Police have urged bank customers to exercise caution when conducting financial transactions, particularly when withdrawing large sums of money or leaving banking premises.

items.description: …Former minister mobilises supporters for APC in Oyo, dumps PDP/APM alliance By Adeola Badru Former Minister of State for the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Oloye Jumoke Akinjide, has announced her return to active politics ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Senator Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli. The announcement signals Akinjide’s departure from the PDP/APM alliance and her alignment with the APC ahead of the elections. Her political re-engagement was announced on her behalf by her Special Assistant, Olatundun Leke Gabriel (JP), a former Chief of Staff to the Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly. In a statement, Gabriel expressed appreciation to Akinjide’s political associates, loyal followers and supporters for their continued loyalty, prayers and solidarity over the years. He said the former minister had begun a renewed political journey, urging her supporters across Oyo State and beyond to remain united and committed. The statement read: “On behalf of my Principal, Oloye Jumoke Akinjide, former Minister of State, FCT, I wish to express our profound gratitude for your unwavering love, loyalty, prayers and continuous support over the years. “We are pleased to announce that the journey to renewed service has begun.” It added that Akinjide was aligning with Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and Alli’s political vision ahead of the 2027 elections. “As we align with the Renewed Hope Agenda of our Leader and Father, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, and with the vision of our Gubernatorial Candidate, Distinguished Senator Sharafadeen Alli, Gubernatorial Candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Oyo State, we urge all supporters across Oyo State and beyond to remain steadfast, united, prayerful and focused,” the statement said. Gabriel said further directives and engagements would be communicated in due course, urging supporters to remain connected and committed. items.title: ‎UniMAC-SOJAMS Level 300 student Jemimah Andoh nominated for GJA Best Student Journalist Award‎
items.description: Jemimah Andoh, a level 300 student of the School of Journalism and Media Studies (SOJAMS) at the University of Media, Arts and Communication (UniMAC), has earned a nomination in the Best Student Journalist category at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards. ‎ ‎Her nomination recognises her journalistic work, including a feature story titled “Vanishing Pesewas,” which was aired on JoyNews on Thursday, July 17, 2025. ‎ ‎The feature examined the issue of disappearing pesewas, highlighting her work as a student journalist and her contribution to public-interest reporting. Ms Andoh is also the Vice President of the Journalism and Media Students Association (JOMSA), an association set up by the School Journalism and Media Studies (SOJAMS) to bring journalism students closer to the school, have their voices heard and offer further professional development and growth beyond the classroom. ‎ ‎ ‎The nomination comes ahead of the awards ceremony scheduled for Saturday, November 7, 2026, at the Palms Convention Centre at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel. ‎The 30th edition of the awards will be held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.” ‎ ‎President John Dramani Mahama is expected to attend as a special guest of honour, alongside the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, who is the GJA’s patron. ‎ ‎The Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, will chair the ceremony. ‎ ‎According to the GJA, 327 entries were received from 206 journalists, with the nine-member Awards Committee, chaired by former Daily Graphic Editor Kobby Asmah, reviewing 326 entries across the various categories. ‎ ‎GJA President Albert Kwabena Dwumfour said the 30th anniversary edition would celebrate journalists and media organisations whose work had contributed to Ghana’s democratic governance, national development and public accountability. ‎ ‎The ceremony will recognise outstanding journalism across television, radio, print, online and digital media, with the prestigious P.A.V. Ansah Journalist of the Year Award among the major honours to be presented. ‎ ‎Other nominees include Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe of JoyNews; Philip Osei Bonsu of Asempa FM; Nana Boakye Yiadom of JoyNews and Asempa Dawuro; and Emmanuel Adu Gyamfi of JoyNews and Asempa. items.title: Importations des viandes : nouvelle exigence de l’Algérie
items.description: La grande mosquée de Paris (GMP), à travers son institut islamique, a l’exclusivité depuis décembre 2022 de certifier tous les produits halal importés par l’Algérie de France ou tout autre pays. Quatre ans après, cette obligation fait l’objet d’un rappel aux opérateurs économiques par le ministère du Commerce intérieur et de Régulation du marché national. Les mêmes services ont imposé une nouvelle disposition concernant les certificats Halal des viandes importées. Certification halal en Algérie : la Grande mosquée de Paris a toujours l'exclusivité Les opérateurs économiques et leurs représentants dûment habilités sont informés que, conformément aux dispositions de l'instruction en vigueur relative aux certificats Halal, ces certificats doivent obligatoirement être établis par la Grande Mosquée de Paris ou par l'un de ses bureaux agréés implantés dans le pays d'exportation. Le rappel est contenu dans une note de l'inspection aux frontières du port de Béjaïa, relevant du ministère du Commerce intérieur qui a joint en annexe la liste des bureaux agréés. Importation de viandes : la spécification du sexe de l’animal obligatoire Dans la même note, il est indiqué que le certificat Halal doit obligatoirement comporter le nom ou la raison sociale de l'importateur en Algérie ainsi qu'une disposition spéciale pour l’importation de viandes. Le certificat doit désormais obligatoirement spécifier le type d'animal ainsi que son sexe. Les opérateurs économiques et leurs représentants sont invités à veiller au strict respect de ces exigences et à s'assurer de la conformité des certificats Halal avant la présentation des dossiers concernés aux services de contrôle, afin d'éviter tout retard dans les procédures de traitement des dossiers d'importation, indique l’inspection aux frontières du port de Béjaïa. L’exclusivité de la certification halal a été octroyée en décembre 2022 à la mosquée de Paris par le ministère des Affaires étrangères et des Wakfs. La disposition est entrée en vigueur en juin 2023. La décision a été critiquée en France notamment par certaines figures du courant anti-algérien, comme Bruno Retailleau. Alors qu'il était ministre de l’intérieur, Retailleau a accusé la GMP d’avoir mis en place “un juteux système financier” après avoir obtenu du gouvernement algérien l'exclusivité de la certification Halal “. L’article Importations des viandes : nouvelle exigence de l'Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the leadership of the Department of State Services, DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally. Atiku said the alleged plot was part of a broader attempt by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to frustrate opposition parties, undermine political competition and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose their leaders ahead of the 2027 general election. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, the former vice president alleged that public facilities meant for campaign activities had been blocked and logistical support withheld in Sokoto, describing the developments as deliberate efforts to deny the ADC a level playing field. He said information available to the party indicated that protesters were being mobilised from an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road, with trucks deployed to strategic locations, including a roundabout. According to him, the protesters were causing gridlock, threatening commuters and beating some residents, while some had moved away from the roundabout to find shade. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform,” Atiku said. “Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis.” He called on security officers allegedly involved in the mobilisation to stop immediately and return to their constitutional duty of impartial service. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of devoting much of its energy over the past three and a half years to weakening credible opposition, alleging that its strategy of absorbing former opposition figures into the APC was aimed at reducing Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name. The former vice president also linked the alleged obstruction of the rally to the economic hardship facing Nigerians, saying the government should be defending its record on the rising cost of food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials rather than trying to stop opposition campaigns. “Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive,” he said. “That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.” Atiku pledged that an ADC government would make life affordable through policies to support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. He said the party would also pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, aimed at providing measurable relief to consumers while strengthening domestic industry. The ADC presidential candidate accused the APC of resorting to intimidation and obstruction after what he described as the failure of its last rally in Kaduna, saying the party should have taken the outcome as a warning that Nigerians were withdrawing their confidence. “These are the last kicks of a dying horse,” Atiku said. “The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence.” Atiku said the 2027 general election would be a defining moment in Nigeria’s democratic history, insisting that the contest was not merely between political parties or candidates but between a government he accused of indifference to citizens’ suffering and Nigerians determined to make their votes count. He vowed that the ADC would resist what he described as administrative roadblocks and underhand manoeuvres designed to exclude the opposition, adding that he would be in Sokoto on Wednesday to address residents. “I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state,” he said. He urged residents to remain peaceful and avoid being provoked into violence, while calling on security agencies to protect commuters, residents and rally participants without favour. Atiku also warned that officers who colluded in suppressing political freedom would be held accountable under the law, while pledging support for those who refused to be used against democracy. He urged Nigerians to remain resolute in defending their democratic rights, declaring that the country belonged to its people and not any political party or temporary occupant of power. items.title: Two NYSC kidnap victims testify against suspects
items.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — Two victims of the abduction of 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) have testified for the prosecution in the ongoing trial of three men accused of involvement in the kidnapping. The victims, identified in court only as Miss A and Miss B for security reasons, testified as the fourth and fifth prosecution witnesses in suit number HOU/22c/2026 against Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu and Mohamed Ali. They gave accounts of how the prospective corps members were abducted while travelling to their NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. Testifying, Miss A told the court that they departed Ibadan on September 30, 2026, stopped over in Onitsha and continued their journey the following morning. She said that about three or four electricity poles after they passed a security checkpoint along the Owerri-Onitsha Road, they heard gunshots. According to her, their driver attempted to reverse but hit the bus behind them before opening his door and fleeing. The witness alleged that Usman Aliyu, who was armed with an AK-47 rifle, took 15 passengers from one bus and five from the other, ordered them to lie on the ground and subsequently led them into the bush. Miss A further narrated how the captives were blindfolded and shackled after their first stop in the forest. She said they were given muddy water to drink when they became thirsty, adding that whenever a helicopter hovered over the area, their captors ordered them to lie flat and remain motionless. The witness said that on the second day of their captivity, the kidnappers allowed them to contact their parents and demanded a ransom of N50 million for each victim, threatening that they would be killed if the money was not paid. She also told the court that the captors instructed them to transfer money into an account, claiming it was meant for the purchase of food. However, the money was allegedly used to buy dry, yellow garri. Miss A, who broke down while narrating her experience, said that after collecting the ransom, the kidnappers shared the money among themselves, gave each captive N2,000 as transport fare and showed them the way out of the forest. She said the victims eventually found their way to the Department of State Services (DSS) office in Owerri, where they made statements and received medical attention. Miss B corroborated the account of the fourth prosecution witness. Following her testimony and cross-examination by defence counsel, Mr Nnaemeka Adipo, prosecuting counsel, Mr Ekezie Nwauzor, announced the closure of the prosecution’s case. Justice Emeka Orafu subsequently adjourned the matter to November 5, 2026, and directed the defence counsel to prepare to open the defendants’ case on that date. items.title: GIS investigates explosion that killed officer during Hamile border patrol
items.description: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is investigating an explosion during a border patrol operation in the Hamile Sector of the Upper West Region that killed one of its officers and a tricycle rider. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, along an unapproved route in the border area, according to a statement issued by the Service. The GIS said a team of four officers on patrol responded to an unusual sound and intercepted a man transporting a load on a tricycle. The rider reportedly attempted to flee as the officers approached to inspect the contents of the load. “In the process of trying to stop him, the load exploded, resulting in the death of the tricycle rider and injuries to two officers,” the statement said. One of the injured officers later died from his injuries, while the other is receiving emergency medical care at Nandom Hospital and is reported to be in stable condition. The GIS said the Sector Commander and a team had visited the scene, which has since been secured. Investigations have commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the explosion. The Service assured the public that border security operations in the Hamile Sector remain fully operational, adding that measures were being taken to maintain safety and security in the area. The Service extended its condolences to the family, colleagues and friends of the deceased officer. It also appealed to the media and the public to respect the privacy of the affected families and refrain from circulating unverified information, images or videos relating to the incident. The GIS said further updates would be communicated as investigations progress.

items.title: Senate steps down Barau’s Agricultural Revolution Bill
items.description: ….Ningi, Yahaya Abdullahi fault drafting, omnibus nature, non-circulation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate on Tuesday stepped down the proposed Agricultural Revolution Bill, 2026, following a heated debate over its drafting, scope and failure to circulate printed copies to senators. The bill, sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), failed to scale second reading after several lawmakers raised concerns about its content and compliance with legislative procedures. Titled “A Bill for an Act to Provide a Comprehensive Legal Framework for Transformation and Modernisation of Agriculture in Nigeria, Promote Food Security, Agricultural Productivity, Mechanisation, Irrigation, Agricultural Financing, Agro-industrialisation, Rural Development and Climate-resilient Farming and for Related Matters,” the proposed legislation seeks to establish a framework for the transformation and sustainable development of the agricultural sector. Presenting its general principles on behalf of Barau, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), said the legislation was necessary to address Nigeria’s food security challenges. Monguno said agriculture provided livelihoods for millions of Nigerians, accounting for about 70 per cent of employment and 40 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product. He identified low productivity, inadequate mechanisation, limited irrigation infrastructure, high post-harvest losses, poor access to affordable financing, insecurity in farming communities and weak agricultural value chains as major challenges confronting the sector. According to him, the challenges had contributed to food insecurity, inflation and rising poverty, making it necessary to move beyond fragmented interventions towards a coordinated legal framework. He said the bill sought to reposition Nigerian agriculture from subsistence production to modern, technology-driven and commercially viable farming through mechanisation, improved seeds, agricultural research, extension services and irrigation development. It also proposed measures to strengthen the agricultural value chain through storage facilities, cold-chain infrastructure, agro-processing and improved market access. Seconding the bill, Senator Adamu Aliero (APC, Kebbi Central) said agriculture remained central to Nigeria’s economic diversification efforts and should be developed as a commercial venture rather than largely subsistence activity. He called for massive investment in mechanisation, research and development to improve agricultural productivity and increase farmers’ yields per hectare. Trouble, however, started when Senator Abdul Ningi (Bauchi Central) raised concerns about the bill’s drafting, although he described its objectives as timely and commendable. Ningi argued that the document presented to the Senate appeared more like a motion than a properly developed legislative proposal. He said Nigerian farmers recorded average yields of between two and three tonnes per hectare, compared with eight to 10 tonnes in other countries, stressing that the gap required substantial investment in mechanisation and agricultural research. While commending the Federal Government’s agreement to import agricultural machinery from Brazil, he said the proposed legislation lacked sufficient details on how its objectives would be achieved. He questioned the need for a new legal framework when existing agencies were already responsible for areas such as irrigation and agricultural mechanisation. “The spirit of this bill is excellent; it is fantastic, and it is also equally timeous. But when you bring a bill that has subsisting agencies in place, existing to take care of irrigation and mechanisation, what you ought to do is to first bring the bill; let’s see the bill. “This looks like a motion. This bill did not say it is creating an agency, this bill did not say it is amending existing agencies that you and everybody knows and are actually meant to take care of certain things. “This is a brilliant idea, but a lot of work has not been done to capture what the Deputy Senate President intends to achieve,” Ningi said. He urged the Senate to step down the bill to allow its sponsor to properly develop its provisions before bringing it back for consideration. Also opposing the proposed legislation, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi (APC, Kebbi North), warned against passing what he described as an overly broad law covering the entire agricultural sector. Abdullahi, who said he had taught agricultural science at a university for more than 25 years before joining the Senate, argued that agriculture was too broad to be effectively regulated under a single omnibus legislation. “Let me be frank. I have been an agricultural teacher in an Agricultural University for more than 25 years before I came to the Senate. Agriculture is too wide and omnibus in human endeavour for it to be covered effectively and efficiently under one single bill or a law,” he said. He argued that issues such as subsidies, mechanisation and irrigation were distinct areas requiring specific legislative attention. He advised lawmakers to identify the particular challenges requiring legislative intervention rather than attempting to address the entire agricultural sector through one law. “Let’s look into the content of our agriculture and identify those areas of constraint where legislation is required and address those particular areas, but to make an omnibus law covering the entire field of agriculture, with due respect, we may be making a fool of ourselves,” he added. In defence of the bill, Monguno explained that the Senate had agreed that proposed legislation should be gazetted and uploaded on its digital platform, while printed copies would be distributed ahead of clause-by-clause consideration. He, however, conceded that if the bill had not been gazetted, its sponsor should be encouraged to withdraw it until the required procedures were completed. Senate President Godswill Akpabio subsequently invited Barau to consider stepping down the bill to address the concerns raised. The Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), also appealed for the bill to be allowed to proceed to second reading, arguing that concerns about its detailed provisions could be addressed during subsequent legislative scrutiny with input from experts. However, Ningi cited Order 77(3) and (4) of the Senate Standing Orders, which provides for the distribution of printed copies of bills to every senator as soon as possible. He insisted that the issue was procedural and not personal. Following the objections, Barau agreed to withdraw the bill temporarily, promising to ensure that printed copies were made available to senators before reintroducing it. “Since that’s what you want, I will get it done. Forget about the fact that it has been placed on the platform. As we agreed, we are going to give you and others who have not gotten it, in compliance with the rules. “I am the Deputy Senate President, I will always want to please anyone to the best of my ability. I don’t think we should belabour ourselves talking about this. I will find time, give it to him, redistribute it and then represent the bill,” he said. Akpabio subsequently acknowledged the withdrawal, bringing the consideration of the proposed legislation to an end for the day. items.title: Ronaldo Jnr. earns first Portugal U17 call-up, could meet father at training ground
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo Jnr. has received his first call-up to Portugal’s Under-17 team, raising the possibility of meeting his father, Cristiano Ronaldo, at the national team’s training base during the November international window. According to ESPN, the 16-year-old Al Nassr academy forward has been named in Filipe Ramos’ 23-man squad for the 2027 European Under-17 Championship qualifying matches, having previously represented Portugal at U15 and U16 levels. The Portuguese footballing icon’s son, known popularly as “Cristianinho” (which translates to “Little Cristiano” in Portuguese), has previously represented the national side in the U-15 and U-16 levels since his debut in May 2025, making 13 appearances across both age group and scoring five goals. Portugal’s U17 team will play Andorra on November 11, Bulgaria on November 14 and Serbia on November 17, with all three matches scheduled to take place at the Portuguese Football Federation’s Cidade do Futebol training complex in Oeiras, near Lisbon. The team’s training camp is also scheduled to run at the facility from November 6 to 17. His father could also be at the same training base if he is included in Portugal’s senior squad for the upcoming international fixtures against Denmark on November 14 and Wales on November 17. However, Cristiano Ronaldo’s participation remains uncertain following reports that he was handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after leaving the national team camp during last month’s Nations League campaign. The 41-year-old remains Portugal’s all-time leading scorer in men’s international football, with 143 goals in 225 appearances. Ronaldo Jnr.’s maiden U17 call-up marks another step in his progression through Portugal’s youth national teams as he continues his development at Al Nassr’s academy. His father, meanwhile, is closing in on the 1,000-goal career milestone, having scored 985 goals. He recently netted a hat-trick for Al Nassr. In the past, Cristiano Ronaldo has spoken well about his son. At the Globe Soccer Awards in December 2020, he shared how his son’s diet and habits sometimes frustrated him, noting that the young boy liked drinking soda and eating crisps or fries even though he had great athletic potential. Ronaldo said: “We’ll see if he’ll be a great player. He’s not yet. Sometimes he drinks coke, he eats fries and he knows I get mad. I tell him to treadmill and then dive into cold water to recover, and he says: “Dad, but it’s so cold.” It’s normal because he’s young. He has potential. He is fast, he dribbles well, but that’s not enough. It takes a lot of hard work and dedication. I’m not going to pressure him to be a player. However, I especially want him to be the best, whether he’s a footballer or a doctor.” Vanguard News The post Ronaldo Jnr. earns first Portugal U17 call-up, could meet father at training ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in US midterm election
items.description: Ballot machines malfunctioned Tuesday in a New York county that will help decide a closely contested House of Representatives race, though officials said votes for the US midterm elections are still being counted. Read Also: Trump cites immigration, Iran, tariffs in election day pitch The Westchester County Board of Elections “is aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county,” a statement read. It “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags. Parts of Westchester County are included in New York’s 17th district, where incumbent Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a Hudson Valley seat won by Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. The New York State Board of Elections said on X that there has been no disruption to voting. “Long-established emergency ballot procedures have been implemented, where completed ballots are secured, under bipartisan control, and will be counted,” it said. President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven conspiracy theories about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable. items.title: Burkina Faso : Deux fiancés décèdent à Tenkodogo après une altercation impliquant une arme à feu
items.description: Une commerçante et un sous-officier des forces de défense et de sécurité, présentés comme fiancés, sont décédés au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Tenkodogo après une altercation survenue dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre 2026 au secteur 6, selon des témoignages recueillis par l'Agence d'information du Burkina (AIB). Les deux victimes, identifiées comme Jeanne Yoda et Adama Tiendrébéogo, auraient eu une dispute aux abords d'une pharmacie, non loin de l'hôpital. D'après les riverains, les échanges auraient dégénéré en affrontement physique avant que la commerçante ne quitte les lieux à scooter pour regagner son domicile. Toujours selon ces témoignages, le sous-officier l'aurait poursuivie et aurait ouvert le feu sur elle. Grièvement blessée, Jeanne Yoda a été évacuée au CHR, où elle a succombé à ses blessures. Le militaire aurait ensuite retourné son arme contre lui-même. Transporté dans un état critique au même établissement, il est décédé dans l'après-midi du 2 novembre. L'AIB précise qu'au moment de la publication de sa dépêche, aucune communication officielle des autorités sécuritaires ou judiciaires n'avait été faite. Les circonstances exactes du drame, notamment les conditions de l'usage de l'arme, restent donc à établir par les enquêtes. Lefaso.net Source : AIB

Bourse de Casablanca : clôture en territoire négatif
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a clôturé en territoire négatif mardi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,76% à 16.390,89 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a avancé de 0,1% à 1.196,95 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, s'est adjugé 2,2% à 1.257 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a, quant à lui, perdu 0,01% à 1.558,85 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Mines » (-6,76%), « Sylviculture et papier » (-4,03%) et « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (-3,11%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+3,94%), « Pétrole et gaz » (+3,6%) et « Télécommunications » (+1,18) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 1,65 milliard de dirhams (MMDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché des blocs et dominés par les transactions sur Managem (195,91 millions de dirhams (MDH)), Attijariwafa Bank (24,08 MDH) et Addoha (12,72 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est, quant à elle, établie à plus de 961,72 MMDH. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par Managem (-8,05% à 1.370 DH), Eqdom (-5,93% à 1.364 DH), Med Paper (-4,03% à 21,45 DH), AtlantaSanad (-3,93% à 110 DH) et SMI (-3,74% à 4.861 DH). En revanche, les plus fortes hausses ont été enregistrées par Douja Prom Addoha (+5,23% à 36,20 DH), Afriquia Gaz (+4,5% à 3.460 DH), Résidences Dar Saada (+4,38% à 167 DH), Minière Touissit (+3,69% à 3.600 DH) et Lesieur Cristal (+2,76% à 298 DH). items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Eden Kazoum passe le premier cap en équitation
items.description: La cavalière sénégalaise Eden Kazoum a franchi, mardi, la première étape des épreuves de saut d’obstacles aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Âgée de 15 ans, l’unique représentante du Sénégal dans cette discipline s’est classée cinquième à l’issue de la première phase qualificative, décrochant ainsi son billet pour la suite de la compétition. Engagée au Centre équestre de Diamniadio, la jeune Sénégalaise a bouclé son parcours en 85 secondes et 43 centièmes, avec quatre points de pénalité. Sur les 24 cavaliers annoncés au départ, elle figure parmi les concurrents qui poursuivent l'aventure olympique. Le cavalier indien Sresht Raju Mantena a dominé cette première épreuve avec un parcours sans faute, réalisé en 83 secondes et 36 centièmes. Cette qualification vient récompenser le parcours prometteur d’Eden Kazoum. Championne du Sénégal junior en 2025, elle s'était également illustrée en janvier 2026 en remportant le Grand Prix de saut d’obstacles des Écuries Hann Marinas, en Nationale 2. La jeune cavalière avait déjà décroché sa qualification pour les JOJ à l'occasion du World Jumping Challenge en mai 2025, alors qu'elle n'avait que 13 ans. Elle avait notamment obtenu le certificat de capacité de la Fédération équestre internationale (FEI), lui permettant de représenter le Sénégal à cette compétition. À Dakar, Eden Kazoum porte ainsi les espoirs de l'équitation sénégalaise sur une scène olympique historique. Au-delà de sa performance sportive, elle contribue également à faire découvrir au public une discipline encore peu médiatisée au Sénégal. Dans une séquence consacrée aux coulisses du saut d’obstacles, elle partage son expérience et permet de mieux comprendre les exigences de cette discipline, où la précision du cavalier, la maîtrise du parcours et la complicité avec le cheval sont essentielles. La compétition se poursuit avec les prochaines phases qualificatives avant la finale prévue le 6 novembre.

items.title: 2027: Thousands storm Ebonyi streets, declare support for Tinubu’s re-election
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo Ahead of the 2027 general elections, thousands of supporters of President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday staged solidarity marches across Ebonyi State, declaring support for his re-election and that of Governor Francis Nwifuru. The protesters, under the aegis of Ebonyi United Forum, were mobilised to counter what they described as sponsored anti-Tinubu protests. The marchers, estimated by organisers at 20,000, carried placards with inscriptions such as “Tinubu Beyond 2027”, “Tinubu Must Stay” and “We Believe in Tinubu”, while chanting solidarity songs for the President, Nwifuru and the All Progressives Congress (APC). Addressing the protesters in Abakaliki, Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, thanked them for demonstrating support for Tinubu, describing those behind the anti-government protests as misguided political opportunists seeking relevance. Umahi argued that the opposition lacked a credible campaign message against Tinubu, whose reforms, he said, were repositioning the country for growth. Earlier, the leader of the march, Comrade Chinedu Nwali, said the rally was organised to reject what he described as political distractions and campaigns of calumny against Tinubu’s administration. Nwali said Ebonyi youths would defend the President’s administration, insisting that the South-East had benefited from federal projects executed under Tinubu, particularly through the Ministry of Works. He declared that Ebonyi was firmly behind Tinubu’s re-election bid and would not provide a platform for anti-government protests. “While other states may be sitting on the fence, Ebonyians are not. We must show appreciation for the numerous projects Mr President has brought to the South-East and Nigeria through our son, the Minister of Works,” Nwali said. He also pledged support for Umahi and Nwifuru, warning against what he described as politically motivated attacks on the trio. items.title: CdM 2030 : les précisions de Fouzi Lekjaa sur les avantages fiscaux
items.description: Les États-Unis avaient souhaité soumettre à l’impôt les primes versées aux sélections participant au Mondial 2026, dont les 20 millions de dollars attribués au Maroc, a révélé Fouzi Lekjaa. Devant les députés, le ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Performance publique a également détaillé les exonérations fiscales prévues pour la Coupe du monde 2030, ainsi que le mécanisme du Fonds d’héritage de la FIFA, doté d’environ 100 millions de dollars au profit du pays organisateur. Les préparatifs du Mondial 2030 ne se limitent pas à la construction et à la rénovation des stades. Ils comportent également un important volet fiscal et financier, dont Fouzi Lekjaa a présenté plusieurs éléments devant la Commission des finances et du développement économique à la Chambre des représentants, mardi 3 novembre, dans le cadre de la poursuite de l’examen détaillé du projet de loi de finances 2027. Le ministre est notamment revenu sur une question qui avait suscité des discussions lors de la dernière Coupe du monde : la fiscalité applicable aux primes financières versées aux sélections nationales. Selon ses explications, les États-Unis souhaitaient soumettre ces montants à l’impôt lors du Mondial 2026. La prime de 20 millions de dollars obtenue par la sélection marocaine aurait ainsi été concernée par cette mesure. Des discussions entre la FIFA et le pays organisateur ont finalement permis de maintenir le régime d’exonération appliqué lors des précédentes éditions de la compétition. Le Maroc a donc échappé à une taxation de cette prime, a indiqué Lekjaa devant les parlementaires. Des exonérations fiscales limitées à la durée du Mondial Abordant les dispositions fiscales prévues pour l’organisation de la Coupe du monde 2030, le responsable gouvernemental a expliqué que les avantages accordés concernent plusieurs impôts et taxes : l’impôt sur les sociétés, l’impôt sur le revenu, la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) ainsi que les droits d’enregistrement. Ces exonérations tiennent notamment au statut de la FIFA, présentée comme une association à but non lucratif. Selon Lekjaa, l’instance internationale ne vient pas s’installer dans le pays hôte pour y créer des entreprises ou développer des activités commerciales, mais pour organiser une manifestation sportive internationale en mobilisant des moyens techniques, humains et logistiques. Le dispositif vise également à éviter les situations de double imposition. Plusieurs intervenants mobilisés pour la compétition perçoivent leurs rémunérations et indemnités dans leurs pays d’origine. De même, des équipements et du matériel sont acheminés temporairement dans les pays organisateurs pour être utilisés pendant le tournoi. Le ministre a toutefois insisté sur le caractère strictement encadré de ces avantages. Les exonérations sont limitées dans le temps et dans l’espace et concernent exclusivement les activités liées à l’organisation de la Coupe du monde. Elles prennent fin avec la manifestation, après quoi le régime fiscal ordinaire retrouve son application. © Mounir Mehimdate Un Fonds d’héritage de 100 millions de dollars Fouzi Lekjaa a également apporté des précisions sur le mécanisme du « Fonds d’héritage » (Fonds d’héritage), à travers lequel la FIFA prévoit de consacrer environ 100 millions de dollars au pays organisateur. Cette enveloppe bénéficie, selon les explications du ministre, d’une exonération fiscale afin de permettre à l’État de mobiliser ces ressources au profit du développement du football. Les fonds doivent notamment contribuer à la modernisation des infrastructures sportives, à la mise à niveau des stades et au soutien des jeunes ainsi que du sport national. Le mécanisme permet ainsi de consacrer une partie des retombées de la compétition au développement durable de l’écosystème sportif du pays hôte. Pour Lekjaa, l’organisation du Mondial constitue un accélérateur de développement qui concerne plusieurs secteurs, et non uniquement le football. Les investissements engagés dans le cadre de cet événement doivent accompagner les projets de transport, les infrastructures, les services publics et les capacités d’accueil du Royaume. Six stades au Maroc, 172 sites concernés par le cahier des charges Le ministre a par ailleurs rappelé la configuration particulière de l’édition 2030. La compétition sera principalement organisée par le Maroc, l’Espagne et le Portugal, tandis que l’Uruguay, l’Argentine et le Paraguay accueilleront des rencontres commémoratives à l’occasion du centenaire de la Coupe du monde. Les premières répartitions actuellement retenues prévoient six stades au Maroc, onze en Espagne et trois au Portugal. Lekjaa a précisé que les besoins de la compétition dépassent toutefois les seules enceintes destinées à accueillir les matchs. Avec 48 sélections participantes, il faudra également prévoir des infrastructures d’entraînement et des lieux d’hébergement adaptés à chaque équipe. Le cahier des charges comprend ainsi plus de 172 sites, regroupant les villes hôtes et les installations destinées aux préparatifs des sélections. Au Maroc, les stades seront répartis entre Agadir, Marrakech, Casablanca, Rabat, Tanger et Fès. D’autres villes, dont Benslimane et El Jadida, pourront accueillir des équipes pour leurs séances d’entraînement. Cette organisation doit permettre d’étendre les retombées de la compétition à plusieurs territoires, y compris ceux qui ne recevront pas de rencontres officielles. © Mounir Mehimdate Transport, aéroports et capacités hôtelières : les autres chantiers Sur le volet des infrastructures, Lekjaa a souligné que les préparatifs du Mondial doivent s’inscrire dans la continuité du programme de développement national. Il a notamment évoqué le déploiement de lignes de trains régionaux express (RER) sur plusieurs axes : Casablanca-Settat, Rabat-Salé-Kénitra, Marrakech-Safi et Tanger-Tétouan. Le développement des infrastructures aéroportuaires figure également parmi les priorités, afin de répondre à l’augmentation attendue des flux de visiteurs et de supporters. Le programme prévoit aussi la rénovation des anciens stades nationaux selon les normes internationales et la construction du Grand Stade de Casablanca à Benslimane, que le ministre a présenté comme l’une des infrastructures majeures attendues dans le cadre du tournoi. Les exigences concernent également les télécommunications et le secteur de la santé. Lekjaa a notamment évoqué la nécessité de disposer de centres hospitaliers universitaires (CHU) dans chaque région, en plus du renforcement des capacités d’hébergement touristique. Sur ce dernier point, le cahier des charges impose, selon les chiffres avancés par le ministre, la disponibilité d’au moins 72.000 chambres d’hôtel et de 122 établissements hôteliers. Les dispositifs de sécurité et l’aménagement de zones dédiées aux supporters, les « Fan zones », font également partie des conditions à satisfaire. À travers ces différents chantiers, le gouvernement entend inscrire l’organisation du Mondial 2030 dans un programme d’investissements dépassant le cadre de l’événement sportif. Les infrastructures de transport, les équipements sanitaires, les capacités touristiques et les installations sportives sont appelés à répondre aux besoins de la compétition, mais aussi à accompagner les ambitions de développement du Royaume à plus long terme. items.title: Petrosol targets business expansion in 2027, eyes stronger corporate partnerships
items.description: Petrosol Ghana, a leading Oil Marketing Company (OMC), is targeting business expansion in 2027 through stronger corporate partnerships and increased commercial activities. The company’s Head of Marketing, Philip Boamah Assampong, said Petrosol would leverage its existing business relationships to explore new opportunities and strengthen its market presence. He made the remarks on Tuesday, November 3, after leading a delegation from the company to meet the leadership of the Multimedia Group Limited. Mr Assampong said Petrosol currently operates 109 service stations across the country and also supplies fuel and lubricants to mining companies and other corporate institutions. He indicated that the company was looking at expanding its business engagements in the coming year, adding that its relationship with the Multimedia Group would be important in pursuing those ambitions. “We are also in the commercial business space where we supply fuel and lubricant to the mining businesses and then also other companies. So there’s a lot that we’ll do together,” he said. He said the company would continue investing in quality products and customer service while exploring opportunities to grow its operations. Mr Assampong also expressed appreciation to the Multimedia Group for its support over the years, particularly in providing coverage for the company’s corporate social responsibility initiatives.
