items.title: Petrosol to roll out new customer packages ahead of Christmas
items.description: Petrosol Ghana is preparing to introduce new promotional offers and customer packages ahead of the Christmas festivities as part of efforts to reward customers and strengthen loyalty. The company’s Head of Marketing, Philip Boamah Assampong, said the initiatives would be unveiled in the coming weeks. He disclosed this on Tuesday, November 3, after leading a delegation from Petrosol to meet the leadership of The Multimedia Group Limited to strengthen the commercial relationship the two firms has. Mr Assampong said the packages would offer customers additional benefits as they purchase fuel and lubricants and patronise the company’s convenience retail shops. “For our customers, yes, we are coming up with something and within maybe a few weeks they will hear from us. And then also we have some goodies for them,” he said. He encouraged motorists and other customers to continue patronising Petrosol, assuring them of quality fuel, lubricants and improved customer service. He stressed that customer satisfaction remained central to the company’s operations, noting that good products must be matched with quality service to retain customer confidence. “A business cannot exist without customers. So they are our key partners that we really, really want to say we cherish them and want to appreciate them for the support that they have given to Petrosol all these years,” he said.

items.title: Linsan/Kindia : 234 victimes d’accidents enrégistrés en neuf mois, les autorités régionales tirent la sonnette d’alarme
items.description: La recrudescence des accidents de la circulation sur l’axe Kindia-Linsan suscite une vive inquiétude au sein des autorités administratives de la région. Entre janvier et septembre 2026, pas moins de 234 victimes d’accidents ont été recensées sur ce tronçon routier, dont quatre décès enregistrés sur place, selon les données communiquées par le responsable du centre de santé de Linsan. Face à ce bilan préoccupant, les autorités régionales ont décidé de passer à l’action. Le gouverneur de la région administrative de Kindia, accompagné du préfet de Kindia, le colonel Abdourahamane Keïta, ainsi que de plusieurs responsables des services concernés, a effectué une mission d’inspection sur cet axe, couvrant environ 83 kilomètres jusqu’à Linsan. Cette descente sur le terrain avait pour objectif d’identifier les principales causes des accidents et de proposer des solutions concrètes pour renforcer la sécurité des usagers de la route. Au cours de cette visite, le préfet de Kindia a particulièrement pointé du doigt les comportements irresponsables de certains conducteurs, notamment le non-respect du Code de la route. Il a également attiré l’attention sur le déficit de panneaux de signalisation dans plusieurs localités traversées par cet axe. Le colonel Abdourahamane Keïta estime que la prévention des accidents passe nécessairement par un changement de comportement des conducteurs, mais aussi par l’amélioration des infrastructures et des dispositifs de sécurité routière. Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité de libérer les emprises de la route afin d’éloigner les installations et les populations de la chaussée, tout en améliorant la visibilité des automobilistes. Le responsable préfectoral a également appelé les syndicats des transporteurs à jouer pleinement leur rôle dans la sensibilisation de leurs membres, en mettant un accent particulier sur le respect de la signalisation, la maîtrise de la vitesse et la prudence dans les virages. « Ce ne sont pas des moutons qui sont dans les véhicules, ce sont des êtres humains qui y sont transportés. Il faut considérer ces vies humaines et respecter les règles de conduite », a-t-il rappelé avec insistance. Par ailleurs, le renforcement des moyens opérationnels de la gendarmerie routière figure parmi les préoccupations soulevées au cours de cette mission. Le préfet a plaidé pour une dotation supplémentaire en équipements et en moyens de déplacement afin de permettre aux agents d’assurer efficacement les contrôles, y compris dans les zones les plus éloignées. La mission a connu la participation des forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que des représentants du ministère des Transports. Elle traduit la volonté des autorités de mobiliser l’ensemble des acteurs concernés autour d’une stratégie commune de prévention et de lutte contre l’insécurité routière. Avec 234 victimes recensées en seulement neuf mois, l’axe Kindia-Linsan apparaît plus que jamais comme un tronçon nécessitant une attention particulière. Pour les autorités, l’urgence est désormais de transformer les constats effectués sur le terrain en actions concrètes afin de préserver les vies humaines et de mettre un frein à cette série d’accidents.

items.title: Pologne : Tusk annonce un important déploiement sécuritaire à la frontière avec la région russe de Kaliningrad après le signalement de « personnes avec des lampes de poche »
items.description: Le Premier ministre polonais Donald Tusk a declare, le 3 novembre, avoir renforce la presence des forces de securite a la frontiere avec la region russe de Kaliningrad, apres un signalement nocturne de mouvements consideres comme suspects par les gardes-frontieres. a l'ouverture du Conseil des ministres, il a explique avoir ete informe, apres minuit, de la presence de « personnes avec des lampes de poche ». Les autorites ont alors rapidement mobilise des moyens supplementaires. « Nous avons reussi a empecher des tentatives de provocation, si tant est qu'il y en ait eu », a-t-il precise. Une declaration qui laisse toutefois ouverte la question de l'existence meme des provocations. Si Varsovie met en avant la rapidite de sa reaction, aucun element rendu public ne permet d'etablir une quelconque activite hostile. La presence de personnes munies de lampes de poche figure ainsi comme l'argument avance pour expliquer l'ampleur du dispositif deploye. Un dispositif fonde sur des menaces non confirmees Le renforcement annonce par Tusk s'inscrit dans une operation engagee la veille dans la zone frontaliere. Presentee des le 2 novembre par le chef de la police polonaise Marek Boron, celle-ci repose sur des avertissements de certains services de renseignement concernant de possibles actes de sabotage ou de provocation debut novembre. Les autorites font etat du risque d'une infiltration a travers la frontiere. Le scenario reste cependant hypothetique, aucun indice concret n'etant venu en confirmer la preparation. Varsovie a neanmoins depeche d'importants moyens, notamment des policiers, des gardes-frontieres et des unites antiterroristes. Des membres des forces speciales GROM auraient aussi ete envoyes sur place pour surveiller la situation. Kaliningrad au centre des tensions L'operation concerne les voïvodies de Varmie-Mazurie et de Podlachie. Un etat-major special, installe au sein de la Direction generale de la police, coordonne les interventions avec l'armee, les gardes-frontieres et les services de renseignement. Les autorites polonaises decrivent les mesures comme preventives et destinees a proteger la population et les infrastructures. Des renforts ont ete transferes depuis plusieurs regions du pays, sans precision sur les effectifs engages. Le deploiement intervient alors que la Pologne poursuit la montee en puissance de ses capacites militaires pres de la region de Kaliningrad. Varsovie prevoit entre autres de transformer une brigade de defense territoriale en unite specialement chargee de la protection de la frontiere avec la region russe. Les initiatives s'inscrivent dans un climat de frictions persistantes entre Moscou et l'OTAN. La Russie exprime regulierement ses preoccupations face a l'intensification des activites militaires de l'Alliance atlantique a proximite de son territoire et rappelle que Kaliningrad fait partie integrante de la Federation de Russie. Le president Vladimir Poutine a plusieurs fois affirme que Moscou ne recherchait pas de confrontation avec l'OTAN, tout en avertissant que le pays utiliserait les moyens necessaires pour repousser toute eventuelle agression.

items.title: Petrosol, Multimedia Group move to strengthen commercial partnership
items.description: Petrosol Ghana, a leading Oil Marketing Company (OMC), is seeking to deepen its commercial relationship with the Multimedia Group Limited as both companies explore opportunities for further collaboration. The move formed part of a visit by a delegation from Petrosol, led by its Head of Marketing, Philip Boamah Assampong, to the leadership of the Multimedia Group on Tuesday, November 3. Ken Ansah, Chief Operating Officer (COO) and David Max-Fugar, General Manager for Sales of the Multimedia Group Limited, received the OMC and had a dialogue on how to build on the existing relationship between the two firms. Mr Assampong said the visit was intended to appreciate the media company’s longstanding support for Petrosol and explore ways to build on their existing relationship for mutual business growth. He described the Multimedia Group as a valued partner, particularly for its support in publicising the company’s activities, including its corporate social responsibility initiatives. “We thought it wise to visit them, to say hello to them and then also to appreciate them for their support to Petrosol all these years,” he said. He added that the company was interested in leveraging the relationship to explore further business opportunities as it positions itself for growth in 2027. Petrosol currently operates 109 service stations across the country and provides fuel and lubricants to mining companies and other corporate institutions. Mr Assampong said the company remained committed to expanding its commercial operations while maintaining strong relationships with its business partners and customers. He also expressed appreciation to Petrosol’s customers for their continued patronage, assuring them of quality products and improved service delivery. The engagement is expected to provide an opportunity for both companies to identify areas of mutual interest and strengthen their existing commercial ties.

items.title: NDC to lose 29 seats, NPP to gain 12 in 2028 elections – Global InfoAnalytics projects
items.description: A new projection by Global InfoAnalytics has revealed that the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) could see its parliamentary representation decline, while the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) is projected to gain seats in the 2028 parliamentary elections. The research organisation’s first parliamentary seat projection for the 2028 general elections estimates that the NPP will increase its current 88 seats to 100, while the NDC’s representation could fall from 185 to 154 seats. Despite the projected decline, the NDC is expected to retain a majority in Parliament, with the model assigning it 55.8 per cent of the total seats, compared with 36.2 per cent for the NPP. However, the projection leaves 22 constituencies without a definitive outcome. Of these, 20 have been classified as “not disclosed”, while the remaining two are considered toss-ups. The Eastern Region has the highest number of undisclosed constituencies, with five, followed by the Ashanti Region with four. The Western Region accounts for three, while the Upper East has two. Central, Greater Accra, Oti, Upper West, Western North and Bono regions each have one constituency in the undisclosed category. The two toss-up constituencies are in the Ashanti and Bono regions and could go either way. The 20 undisclosed seats represent 7.2 per cent of Parliament, while the two toss-up constituencies account for 0.7 per cent. The projection, which uses Global InfoAnalytics’ Multilevel Regression and Poststratification (MRP) model, suggests that the NDC could face a reduced parliamentary majority in 2028 if the estimates materialise. However, the projections, generated using its MRP model, are estimates and should not be taken as a definitive indication of the outcome of the 2028 parliamentary elections. The research firm noted that voting preferences in the 20 undisclosed constituencies have not been made public, while the two toss-up seats remain too close to call.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Closing performance gaps before year-end
items.description: Insight. Every organisation experiences a gap between planned performance and actual results. The CEO’s responsibility is to identify these gaps early enough and ensure that corrective action is taken before they become permanent year-end shortfalls. Closing performance gaps requires more than demanding better results. CEOs must understand the underlying causes, whether they relate to weak execution, insufficient resources, operational inefficiencies, changing market conditions, or leadership shortcomings. The objective is to address the causes of underperformance rather than simply manage the symptoms. Key Strategies: Compare actual performance with annual targets and approved budgets. Identify the root causes of significant performance gaps. Prioritize corrective actions based on business impact and urgency. Assign clear ownership and deadlines for improvement initiatives. Monitor corrective actions and adjust them when results are insufficient. CEO Leadership Actions. Require executives to provide evidence explaining major performance shortfalls. Direct management attention towards gaps with the greatest financial and strategic consequences. Regularly review corrective actions until measurable improvements are achieved. Actionable Tip. Ask each executive: “What is the most significant performance gap under your responsibility, what is causing it, and what specific action will close it before December 31?” Why This Matters? Unresolved performance gaps can weaken profitability, customer confidence, employee morale, and strategic execution. CEOs who act early create opportunities for recovery, improve resource utilization, and reduce the risk of carrying avoidable weaknesses into 2027. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: Deputy Works Minister urges business leaders to strengthen project delivery accountability
items.description: Deputy Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources, Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, has urged chief executives and business leaders to strengthen project planning, leadership accountability and implementation oversight to improve the delivery of development projects. She said successful project delivery required more than initiating projects, stressing the importance of adequate preparation, clearly defined responsibilities and continuous monitoring. Speaking at the PM Executive Summit organised by the Project Management Institute (PMI), she urged institutions to identify potential risks early, track project milestones and address implementation challenges before they escalated. “One of the most important responsibilities of leadership is to establish a culture in which commitments are matched by action and performance is assessed against clear standards,” she said. She added that leaders must be willing to make difficult decisions, learn from setbacks and adjust strategies when circumstances change. Ms Tetteh-Agbotui said these principles were particularly important in the works, housing and water resources sectors, where delays, cost overruns, poor coordination and inadequate supervision could have far-reaching consequences. “As the Ministry responsible for Works, Housing and Water Resources, we recognise the importance of these principles in delivering works, housing and water interventions,” she said. She described project preparation as a critical stage of implementation and called on stakeholders to provide the necessary support throughout the project cycle to ensure that initiatives achieve their intended objectives. Managing Director of PMI Sub-Saharan Africa, George Asamani, also stressed the need for thorough preparation before projects commence. He said project initiation must be supported by proper planning and the necessary groundwork, noting that the quality of preparation was a key determinant of successful implementation. Mr Asamani urged stakeholders to pay closer attention to project planning and assess whether the required groundwork had been completed before proceeding with implementation. The discussions at the summit highlighted the responsibility of chief executives and business leaders to translate strategic commitments into measurable results through effective project management, accountability and strong institutional leadership. Participants stressed that successful project delivery depends not only on sound ideas and adequate resources but also on the leadership, discipline and systems needed to turn plans into tangible outcomes.

items.title: L’ONMT déploie un dispositif d’envergure pour accélérer sa conquête du marché britannique
items.description: L’Office National Marocain du Tourisme (ONMT), prend part, du 3 au 5 novembre 2026, au World Travel Market de Londres, l’un des principaux rendez-vous internationaux de l’industrie touristique. L’inauguration a eu lieu ce matin, en présence de Hakim Hajoui, Ambassadeur du Royaume du Maroc au Royaume-Uni, et d’Achraf Fayda, Directeur Général de l’ONMT. Pour cette édition, l’Office déploie un pavillon de 850 m² réunissant 47 co-exposants, témoignant de la mobilisation des professionnels marocains autour des ambitions de développement sur le marché britannique. Grandes enseignes hôtelières, groupes nationaux et internationaux, agences de voyages, réceptifs et spécialistes du tourisme d’affaires composent cette délégation. La dimension territoriale occupe également une place centrale avec la participation de huit Conseils Régionaux du Tourisme : Marrakech-Safi, Agadir Souss-Massa, Fès-Meknès, Casablanca-Settat, Rabat-Salé-Kénitra, Drâa-Tafilalet, Béni Mellal-Khénifra et Dakhla-Oued Eddahab. Marrakech-Safi et Agadir Souss-Massa sont particulièrement mises à l’honneur, deux destinations locomotives du marché britannique. Cette mobilisation associe également les principales organisations professionnelles, représentées notamment par la Confédération Nationale du Tourisme, la Fédération Nationale de l’Industrie Hôtelière, et la Fédération Nationale des Agences de Voyages du Maroc. Cette participation intervient dans un contexte de croissance soutenue du marché britannique. À fin août 2026, le Maroc a accueilli 995 663 touristes britanniques, en progression de 7 %, générant près de 3,4 millions de nuitées. En intégrant l’Irlande, les arrivées atteignent 1 065 715 visiteurs. La dynamique repose notamment sur le développement de la connectivité aérienne. Huit compagnies relient aujourd’hui douze aéroports britanniques à huit destinations marocaines. Pour les saisons été 2026 et hiver 2026-2027, la capacité programmée atteint 1,97 million de sièges, en hausse de 7 %. Sur le volet commercial, les partenariats de l’ONMT avec les tour-opérateurs, plateformes de réservation et réseaux de distribution portent sur un objectif contractuel prévisionnel de 1 355 000 passagers, soit une progression de 9 %. À Londres, l’ONMT entend capitaliser sur ces performances pour consolider ses partenariats, développer de nouvelles opportunités commerciales et renforcer la visibilité des différentes destinations marocaines. L’objectif étant de convertir le potentiel du marché britannique en nouvelles parts de marché, en nuitées supplémentaires et en retombées économiques pour les territoires du Royaume. items.title: Govt assures public of meeting winter gas demand, hints at 'good news' for fuel prices
items.description: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Tuesday assured the public that the government will make utmost efforts to meet the demand for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) during the winter months. His remarks come as LPG supply has been disrupted due to the closure of Iranian border crossings, resulting in gas cylinders being sold at twice the official rate in the open market. LPG is widely used for rickshaws, but also for cooking and other purposes by those not on the piped gas network. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, Malik said, “Seeing people’s distress and also knowing that from December and January, winter will be at its peak […] even if the most expensive fuel has to be purchased for the piped network, we will bring it in and try to meet demand through LNG (liquefied natural gas).” The minister assured the public that the government will make “utmost efforts” to ensure piped supply of domestic gas for meal times. Besides this, LPG will be needed for other needs and by those without piped connections, he noted. Speaking on fuel prices, Malik recalled the latest reduction and noted that the international market had closed lower on Tuesday. “Even better news will come before us,” he said, regarding Tuesday’s revision of petrol and diesel prices. Under a newly announced arrangement , oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion for 30 days, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. In his press briefing today, Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for LPG. He observed that the country was facing “numerous challenges” regarding the availability of LPG. The minister added that some individuals were trying to exploit the situation after the supply “dried up on our western border”, with consumers being offered LPG at Rs700-800 per kilogramme. Malik elaborated that the total demand for LPG was approximately 2.4 million tonnes, amounting to about 6,500 to 7,000 tonnes per day. Of this, the country locally produces roughly 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes, depending on which crude they use and how much LPG is produced with it, he added. However, “nearly half or more than half” of the demand used to come through the western border, where “difficulties have arisen”, he said. The rest of the demand is fulfilled from two terminals — Engro and SSGC LPG — with a combined storage capacity of around 14,000 tonnes, the minister said. Malik further said that efforts were under way to build the country’s energy security architecture from scratch, regretting that no work had so far been done on fuel storage or refineries. “Before the war, nobody ever paid attention to how Pakistan needs to work on its infrastructure and energy security,” he observed. Recalling that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif chaired a meeting earlier in the day on the matter, he added that the premier was personally spearheading efforts to “rebuild the entire system from scratch”. “The war may certainly have caught us in its crossfire, but it meant we had to set our own house in order, right? We neither worked on storage, nor on refineries, nor on the LPG chain,” Malik remarked. The minister noted that the majority of the world had shifted from pressurised containers to refrigerated and cryogenic cargoes. He lamented that small pressurised ships were not easily available, while Very Large Gas Carriers (VLGCs) could not dock either, just like Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs). “Even if it comes, where do we store it?” Responding to a query, Malik said, “Domestic [demand] comes first and after that, the space we have carved out is only done by restricting it to the three meal times.” He said domestic demand was expected to surge by 400 to 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), so “we will do whatever curtailment we have to accordingly”. The minister said PM Shehbaz had directed that the necessary alternative arrangements for RLNG be made as well for power, adding: “But for November, we are well covered for both requirements.” In his remarks alongside Malik, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar emphasised that the prime minister prioritised the public’s interests and made “strong and bold” decisions, such as the fuel subsidy scheme. Speaking about the LPG sector, he said, “The monopoly has been abolished, the quota system under which a few people engaged in profiteering has been abolished, discretion has been eliminated, the process has been made transparent [and] competition has been introduced.” He noted that PM Shehbaz had directed Malik to draft a plan for LPG supply during the winter and ensure there was no load-shedding during meal times. “Overall, if you look at it, even in the most difficult circumstances, PM Shehbaz has not abandoned the public. Reforms were carried out, structural reforms were introduced, the process was made transparent and the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) started publishing all the details on its website,” Tarar said. ‘To bring competition in sector’ Expanding upon the pricing mechanism, the petroleum minister said that, internationally, Saudi oil giant Aramco determined the LPG price through its contract price (CP), similar to how Platts determined the oil rate. Malik added that the price was issued on a monthly basis, with Ogra notifying the rate. Therefore, “the government does not have much of a role in it”, he said. He stressed the provision of LPG to the public at a “fair” price. “It cannot be that if the price in the international market is Rs1,000, we can provide it locally for Rs500,” he said. The minister explained that Ogra notified the recent increase in the LPG price because Aramco had announced the CP price of $756 per tonne, compared to $540 per tonne in March. Malik lamented that the gas sector was not properly formalised, remarking that the more formal a player was in the LPG market, the more troubled they were because they “could not compete against the informal sector”. “So, the decision made for this is that competition be introduced into this sector, and through competition, efforts be made to import the cheapest possible fuel and its availability to the public at that price should be ensured, no matter what challenges arise.” The minister noted that under the 2016 LPG policy, Ogra was to decide the price for locally produced LPG based on the CP, or the Free On Board (FOB) price, notified by Aramco. He said the situation had been fine since there were no import costs attached under this system. However, as the demand for fuel grew — so much so that 70 per cent of the need was currently being met through imports — the FOB formula did not cover the import cost and people shifted towards the “grey channel” instead of importing. “Therefore, it has now been decided that this sector will be opened up for competition,” he announced. To correct collusion and cartelisation, the government has directed the state’s major companies — Pakistan State Oil Company, SSGC LPG, and Pakistan LNG Limited — to book bulk deals on government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) bases, Malik said. “And they have made a lot of progress in that,” he added.

items.title: LifeTrac Tech, GRATIS Foundation unveil locally assembled tractor to boost farm mechanisation
items.description: LifeTrac Tech Limited and GRATIS Foundation have unveiled the LifeTrac 6G tractor prototype, a locally fabricated machine aimed at improving agricultural mechanisation and strengthening Ghana’s capacity to manufacture and maintain its own farm equipment. The tractor was launched at the GRATIS Foundation Technology Solution Centre in Tema, following a partnership between the two institutions to adapt and manufacture agricultural machinery locally. President of LifeTrac Group Inc. and LifeTrac Tech Limited, John Duse Stager, said the initiative was designed to address challenges farmers face in accessing reliable tractors, including delays in service delivery, frequent breakdowns and difficulties obtaining spare parts. He said farmers needed more than imported equipment, stressing that they required machinery that could be maintained and repaired locally. “A Ghanaian farmer needs more than just a machine dropped off on a truck. They need equipment suited to our soil, a skilled operator who knows the work, a technician nearby who can repair it, and spare parts they can actually get their hands on here at home,” he said. Mr. Stager explained that the LifeTrac 6G was developed around three pillars: open engineering knowledge, local manufacturing and a Machinery-as-a-Service model. Under the service model, smallholder farmers and cooperatives will be able to book mechanised services without having to purchase and maintain an entire tractor. “The farmer gets timely mechanised work without the capital burden, while estates or agribusinesses that prefer to own can purchase the equipment outright,” he said. The tractor, fabricated and assembled at the GRATIS Foundation’s Tema facility, is designed to support land preparation and material handling, with attachments including a plough, rototiller and front loader. It also features a detachable PowerCube hydraulic system that can be used to power other productive equipment, including brick presses and metalworking machines, beyond the farming season. Mr. Stager said the pilot unit passed its functional drive test on August 6, 2026, while loader trials conducted in September demonstrated its ability to collect, lift, carry and discharge heavy materials. He said the project was intended to strengthen Ghana’s ability to build, maintain and improve the machinery used by its farmers. “That is what manufacturing sovereignty means to us: having the engineering drawings on our desks, the skills in our hands, the tooling in our workshops, and the ability to solve our own problems right here in Ghana,” he said. Chief Executive of GRATIS Foundation, Dr. Isaac Adaebsch, said the institution fabricated the tractor’s steel structure and other key components, with more than 15 technicians involved in the process. He said the project demonstrates the potential of local technical expertise when supported by innovation and strategic partnerships. “Today we show Ghana a machine built here, by Ghanaian hands, for Ghanaian farmers,” he said. Dr. Adaebsch noted that agriculture remains central to Ghana’s economy, but access to appropriate and affordable mechanisation remains a challenge for many farmers. Citing a 2022 study, he said 77.6 per cent of farm operations in Ghana were still performed manually. He stressed that the prototype was only the beginning of a process that would require further testing, validation and improvements, as well as the development of production and after-sales support systems. “This prototype is a first step, and the work ahead is testing, validation and improvement. We will also build the production and after-sales support systems that make a machine useful long after the launch,” he said. The two institutions say the next phase will focus on field deployment, performance testing, operator training and the development of a production and maintenance network to support wider adoption across the country.

items.title: Javits’ killing: ‘Condolences are not a policy. Justice is’ – Minority demands sustained US cooperation
items.description: The Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, has called on the government to sustain its engagement with United States authorities to ensure justice for Javits, the Ghanaian teenager who was killed in the US. He said the government must go beyond expressing condolences to the bereaved family and take practical steps to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. Speaking in Parliament on Tuesday, November 3, during the first day of sitting, Mr Afenyo-Markin acknowledged efforts by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ghana’s Permanent Mission in New York to engage the family but insisted that more needed to be done. He said the government must maintain cooperation with American authorities until the case is brought before the courts. “ What we owe this boy. We acknowledge that the Foreign Ministry has spoken. We know that our Permanent Mission in New York has visited the family. “That is right and proper and we, the Minority, acknowledge that. But condolences are not a policy. Justice is and must be,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin urged the government not to allow public attention surrounding the case to fade, warning that sustained diplomatic engagement would be necessary to ensure accountability. “So we make this demand as a Minority of the government. Do not let the cameras leave and the case go cold. Sustain your cooperation with American authorities not for a week but until the proper responsible stand before a court to face justice,” he told Parliament. He further called for the assignment of a dedicated government official to work directly with the New York Police Department and prosecutors in the Bronx to follow developments in the case. The Minority Leader also urged the government to provide practical support to the bereaved family, including legal and consular assistance. He said the government should also assist with arrangements to bring Javits’ body to Ghana for burial, should the family wish to do so. Mr Afenyo-Markin called on the Foreign Ministry to provide regular updates to Parliament on the progress of the case to ensure that the matter remains a national priority. “Assign a dedicated officer to work with the New York Police and the Bronx prosecutors. Stand with the family in practical ways. Legal help, consular help, help to bring Javits home for burial if they wish and report back to this House so that the nation knows where the case stands,” he said. He stressed that the government must remain committed to the pursuit of justice for the teenager and ensure that the circumstances surrounding his death are fully addressed.

items.title: Affaire de la vidéo impliquant une fillette : Fodé Kourouma placé sous mandat, l’instruction en cours (Tribunal pour enfants)
items.description: L’affaire de la récente vidéo devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux, montrant un jeune homme dansant avec une fillette dans des circonstances jugées inappropriées, connaît une évolution judiciaire. Le principal mis en cause, identifié dans plusieurs publications médiatiques comme Fodé Kourouma, a été placé sous mandat, tandis que l’instruction suit son cours. Interpellé par l’Office de protection du genre, de l’enfance et des mœurs (OPROGEM), à la suite de la diffusion des images controversées, le jeune homme fait désormais l’objet de poursuites judiciaires. L’affaire avait suscité une vague d’indignation sur les réseaux sociaux, relançant le débat sur la protection des enfants face aux comportements susceptibles de porter atteinte à leur dignité et à leur intégrité. Interrogé par Guinéenews sur l’évolution de la procédure, le Procureur spécial près le tribunal pour enfants, Dr Cé Avis Gamy, a confirmé que le mis en cause était placé sous mandat et que l’instruction était en cours.« Il est placé sous mandat. L’instruction est en cours », a-t-il brièvement indiqué. Invité à se prononcer sur les sanctions encourues et sur l’attitude que la justice entend adopter face à ce type de comportement, le magistrat a plaidé pour une approche tenant compte de la spécificité de la justice des mineurs et de la nécessité de préserver les possibilités de réinsertion. Selon lui, le jeune mis en cause est poursuivi pour plusieurs chefs d’accusation. Toutefois, le procureur estime que la réponse judiciaire doit également prendre en considération son degré de compréhension des actes qui lui sont reprochés et les perspectives de son avenir. « Quand il a été interpellé, il ne connaissait pas la gravité de ce qu’il était en train de faire. Aujourd’hui, il est plongé dans un remords total », a expliqué Dr Cé Avis Gamy. Le procureur spécial met ainsi en garde contre une sévérité qui pourrait compromettre définitivement l'avenir d'un jeune en situation de démêlés avec la justice. Il estime que la prise en charge de ce dossier exige du tact, de la responsabilité et une certaine mesure. « À force d’être intransigeant, vous risquez de le détruire », a-t-il notamment soutenu, rappelant que ce jeune pourrait, à l’avenir, contribuer au développement du pays dans différentes fonctions et responsabilités. « L a République a besoin de lui. Donc, nous allons le gérer avec tact et beaucoup de responsabilités », a-t-il ajouté.

La cérémonie de levée de corps s’est déroulée à la morgue de l’Hôpital principal de Dakar, en présence des ministres des Forces armées et de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique, ainsi que de plusieurs autorités militaires et civiles. En service à la Légion de Gendarmerie maritime et fluviale (LGMF), les deux hommes ont été décorés, à titre posthume, au grade de chevalier dans l’Ordre national du Lion, en reconnaissance de leur engagement au service de la Nation. La cérémonie a également été marquée par une forte mobilisation des Forces de défense et de sécurité, venues témoigner leur solidarité aux familles endeuillées. Le Haut-commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale et directeur de la Justice militaire, le commandant de la Brigade nationale des sapeurs-pompiers et le directeur général de la Police nationale ont notamment pris part à cet ultime hommage. À travers cette distinction, la Nation salue le sacrifice de deux de ses fils tombés en service. La Gendarmerie nationale a présenté ses condoléances aux familles et aux proches des disparus.

items.title: Gender Ministry swears in Data Review Committee to strengthen household registry
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has constituted a Data Review Committee to strengthen the quality, accuracy and credibility of data generated by the Ghana National Household Registry (GNHR). The committee, which has been sworn in, will serve as a quality assurance body responsible for reviewing, validating and endorsing analytical reports and findings from the Registry before they are shared with stakeholders and the public. Its establishment comes as the GNHR holds information on approximately three million enrolled households across all 16 regions of Ghana. Speaking at the inauguration, the Ministry’s Chief Director, Dr Marian W. A. Kpakpah, said the committee would play an important role in strengthening the Registry’s work and ensuring that reliable data informs decision-making in the social protection sector. She urged members to take their responsibilities seriously and bring their expertise to bear on the committee’s work. The Head of the GNHR, Dr Richard Adjetey, explained that the committee had been established as a formal peer-review body to provide an additional layer of quality assurance for the Registry’s analytical outputs. He said the growing volume of data analysis made it necessary to establish a structured process to ensure that findings were properly reviewed and validated before being shared with government institutions, development partners and the public. The committee will assess the accuracy, consistency, completeness and reliability of GNHR data and analytical findings, identify errors and methodological gaps, and recommend corrective measures. It will also provide technical guidance on data-sharing protocols, analytical tools and capacity building to improve the use of Registry data in evidence-based decision-making. During the meeting, members were introduced to the committee’s Terms of Reference and responsibilities by Daniel Sackey of the GNHR. He also provided an overview of the Registry’s data collection methodology, Proxy Means Test (PMT) indicators and model, questionnaire, key statistical outputs, Registry health indicators and data quality concerns. The presentation outlined the processes and systems underpinning the Registry and the technical areas the committee would be expected to review. The meeting ended with discussions on the committee’s next steps, with members emphasising the importance of sustained collaboration with the GNHR. The committee is expected to begin work by providing technical reviews and guidance to ensure that analytical outputs from the Registry meet the required standards of quality and credibility.

items.title: Bangladesh garment workers stage fourth day of wage protests
items.description: Garment workers in Bangladesh staged a fourth day of wage protests on Tuesday, with police firing tear gas to disperse demonstrators as unrest disrupted factory operations and transport links in the country’s vital export sector. The unrest, which began on Saturday, has intensified despite the government’s move to form a six-member wage board to review pay in Bangladesh’s garment sector, the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China. It comes at a critical time for manufacturers entering the peak production season for spring and summer export orders. The industry employs about 4 million workers, supplies global brands such as H&M, Zara and Gap, and accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country’s export earnings. Clashes were reported across industrial belts around Dhaka, including Ashulia, Gazipur and the capital’s Mirpur area, as workers staged fresh demonstrations and attempted to block major highways. Dozens of people, including several police officers, were injured in the clashes. H&M assessing any potential impact In Ashulia, police fired tear gas and sound grenades after protesters threw bricks and stones at law enforcement personnel, said Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Ashulia Industrial Police. Similar crowd-control measures were used in Dhaka’s Mirpur area, police said. Additional security forces were deployed to contain the unrest, police said. Several factories in Gazipur and Ashulia again suspended operations or declared holidays after nearly 700 factories shut a day earlier. A shattered window is seen on the facade of a garment factory building in Dhaka, Bangladesh on November 3, 2026, after workers threw stones during protests demanding higher minimum wages. — AFP “There are no major disruptions in our supply chain with only a limited number of factories temporarily closed,” H&M told Reuters . “We are assessing any potential impact on our overall production and supply chain.” The Swedish company added it wanted adequate compensation for garment workers and remained committed to improving wages and working conditions. Workers demand higher minimum wage Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), up from the current 12,500 taka, arguing that rising living costs and persistent inflation have eroded their purchasing power. Several factories were also vandalised during the unrest. “It is crucial that brands act immediately and speak out in support of workers’ demands,” said Anne Bienias, from the Clean Clothes Campaign industry advocacy group. Industry officials warn prolonged closures could delay shipments and damage Bangladesh’s reputation as a reliable sourcing hub as it competes with rivals such as Vietnam and India for global apparel orders. The wage dispute comes amid mounting pressure on workers from rising prices. The government formed the wage board on November 1 to review pay in the garment sector, but the move has yet to calm the protests. Factory owners said they are contending with rising operating costs, uncertainty in energy markets linked to conflict in the Middle East, and softer demand in key export markets. They warn that prolonged unrest could disrupt production schedules and jeopardise export orders, while workers continue to press for higher wages and better working conditions.

items.title: NAPO urges journalists to work without fear of violence, intimidation
items.description: Former running mate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh, has called for stronger action against impunity for crimes targeting journalists, warning that media practitioners are increasingly facing threats and intimidation without accountability. Dr Opoku Prempeh, popularly known as NAPO, raised the concern in a Facebook post on Monday, November 2, to mark the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists. He expressed solidarity with journalists in Ghana and across the world who face threats because of their work, stressing the need to protect their freedom to question public officials, investigate sensitive issues and report on matters of public interest. “On this International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, I stand with media professionals in Ghana and across the world who face threats because of their work,” he stated. “Journalists must be able to ask difficult questions and report on matters of public interest without fear of violence or intimidation,” he added. NAPO cautioned against attempts to intimidate journalists over reports that individuals or institutions may find unfavourable. He said disagreements with media publications should be addressed without endangering the safety of journalists. “Even when we disagree strongly with a report, our response must not place a journalist’s safety at risk,” he said. He called for attacks against journalists to be thoroughly investigated and perpetrators held accountable, while victims and their families are given access to justice. “Attacks against journalists must be investigated thoroughly, those responsible held accountable, and victims and their families given access to justice,” he emphasised. The former Energy Minister also urged politicians and public office holders to uphold these principles, including when they are the subject of critical media scrutiny. “Those of us in political and public life must uphold this standard, including when the scrutiny concerns our own parties,” he stated. He stressed that journalists’ safety should never depend on the political interests, affiliations or personal preferences of the individuals and institutions they report on. “Journalists’ safety must never depend on whom their reporting favours or offends,” he added. The International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists is observed annually on November 2 to raise awareness of attacks against media professionals and promote accountability for crimes committed against them.

items.title: BoG flags 20 unlicensed mobile loan apps, warns public against using their services
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has flagged 20 mobile loan applications for operating without the necessary regulatory approval, urging the public to refrain from using their services. The central bank has also warned financial institutions and payment service providers against supporting transactions linked to the unlicensed operators. In a notice dated November 2, the regulator said the applications were operating in violation of its Directive for Digital Credit Service Providers in Ghana, which took effect in September 2025. The affected applications are Active Loan, Boafo Cash, Cediln, Fair Moni, Fast Loan, Halo Loan, Jmoney, Kredi, KudiNow, LendJet, MeCedi, NhyiraCash, Palcash, Quick Eazzy, SikaFlow, SikaNea, Swift Lending, TrustCredit GH, Velzo and Zedvance. According to the Bank of Ghana, the operations of these providers present potential risks relating to the protection of customers’ personal information, consumer rights and adherence to regulatory requirements. The regulator said it was collaborating with the Cyber Security Authority to address illegal activities in the digital lending industry and safeguard borrowers. BoG warns banks, payment providers The central bank has further directed banks, Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions (SDIs) and Payment Service Providers (PSPs) not to facilitate or process financial transactions for the identified unlicensed loan operators. The warning is intended to prevent regulated financial institutions and payment platforms from providing services that could enable unauthorised digital lending businesses to operate. The Bank of Ghana said it would continue engaging relevant state agencies to identify unlicensed operators, investigate their activities and apply appropriate regulatory enforcement measures. It has urged consumers to stay away from loan applications that lack the necessary authorisation and provide information about suspected illegal operators to the central bank. Digital lending sector under increased scrutiny The latest announcement highlights growing regulatory concerns surrounding the expansion of mobile-based lending services, which have made it possible for consumers to access credit through smartphone applications. Although digital lending platforms offer convenient access to loans, operators outside the regulatory system could expose customers to risks involving personal data, lending conditions and inadequate consumer protection. The Bank of Ghana introduced its Directive for Digital Credit Service Providers in September 2025 to establish rules and regulatory requirements for companies offering digital credit services in the country. The latest action forms part of the central bank’s broader efforts to strengthen supervision of the digital lending market, protect consumers and ensure that providers operate within Ghana’s financial regulatory framework.

items.title: GCB Bank crowns customer service month with Maiden Aerobics Fiesta in Accra
items.description: In an effort to deepen customer relationships through experiences beyond financial services, GCB Bank hosted its maiden Aerobics Fiesta in Accra, combining fitness, health awareness and entertainment to reinforce its customer-centred approach to banking. The event, held at the University of Ghana Stadium on Saturday, October 31, formed part of the Bank’s broader efforts to strengthen relationships with its customers while promoting healthy lifestyles and encouraging greater attention to personal well-being. The fiesta featured a range of activities, including aerobics, yoga sessions, health screenings and family-friendly entertainment, providing participants with an opportunity to engage in physical exercise, access health services and interact with the Bank in a relaxed and informal environment. A major highlight of the occasion was a musical performance by popular Ghanaian music group Dope Nation, whose appearance added excitement to the celebration and provided entertainment for participants. The combination of fitness activities, wellness sessions and live music created an atmosphere that brought together people of different backgrounds and age groups, reinforcing the community-oriented nature of the initiative. Beyond the entertainment and physical activities, the event offered customers an opportunity to interact with GCB Bank’s management and employees outside the conventional banking environment. It also provided a platform for customers and staff to connect through shared experiences, with wellness serving as the central focus of the gathering. The initiative marked the grand finale of GCB Bank’s 2026 Customer Service Month celebration, held under the theme ‘The Extra Mile’ , which underscored the Bank’s commitment to putting customers at the centre of its operations and continually improving their banking experience. Through the celebration, the Bank sought to reinforce the importance of customer satisfaction, service excellence and meaningful engagement, while demonstrating its willingness to explore different approaches to building stronger relationships with the people and communities it serves. Speaking on the rationale behind the initiative, GCB Bank’s Chief Marketing, Communications and Customer Experience Officer, Cynthia Ofori-Dwumfuo, said the Aerobics Fiesta was designed to create an opportunity for the Bank to connect with customers on a more personal level while encouraging them to prioritise their health and general well-being. “With this aerobics, we are trying to engage with our customers on a more personal level. We are also encouraging them to take their wellness seriously,” she said. She explained that the initiative reflected the Bank’s understanding that customer relationships should extend beyond routine financial transactions to include activities and experiences that contribute to customers’ broader interests and quality of life. According to her, the fiesta provided an opportunity for customers to interact with the Bank outside the traditional banking environment, fostering a more relaxed atmosphere for engagement while promoting a shared commitment to healthy living. Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo described the event as the maiden edition of the Bank’s Aerobics Fiesta and expressed optimism that it would become a permanent feature of its annual calendar. She said the Bank was encouraged by the prospects of the initiative and intended to build on the experience by introducing more engaging activities that would bring customers closer to the institution. She further stressed that customer centricity remained a fundamental pillar of the Bank’s corporate strategy, explaining that the needs, expectations and satisfaction of customers continued to inform its business decisions and service delivery priorities. “Customer centricity on its own is actually a pillar of our strategy as a bank and where we are going. We understand that we put the customers first with everything,” she said. The emphasis on customer centricity, she noted, was reflected in the Bank’s commitment to continuously reviewing and improving its services to respond to the changing expectations of customers in an increasingly competitive banking environment. With customers becoming more discerning about the quality of service, convenience and overall experience offered by financial institutions, initiatives such as the Aerobics Fiesta provide an additional avenue for banks to maintain meaningful connections with their clientele. Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo assured customers that the Bank would continue to explore innovative ways of strengthening customer engagement, expressing optimism that the maiden Aerobics Fiesta would pave the way for similar initiatives in subsequent years. Reflecting on the Bank’s longstanding contribution to Ghana’s financial sector, she noted that since its establishment in 1953, GCB Bank had consistently evolved to meet changing customer expectations and respond to developments within the banking industry. She added that the Bank would continue to strengthen its products, services and operational processes to deliver improved banking experiences and sustain its commitment to customer satisfaction. The Bank’s focus on customer wellness also reflects a broader approach to corporate engagement, where businesses seek to establish stronger relationships with stakeholders through initiatives that extend beyond their immediate commercial activities. By incorporating physical exercise, health awareness and entertainment into its Customer Service Month celebration, GCB Bank provided a platform for customers, employees and other stakeholders to connect through shared experiences while highlighting the importance of maintaining healthy lifestyles. The event further reinforced the message behind this year’s theme, ‘The Extra Mile’, by demonstrating the Bank’s intention to explore additional ways of engaging customers and making their relationship with the institution more meaningful. As the Bank looks towards future editions of the initiative, the maiden Aerobics Fiesta provided a foundation for expanding its customer engagement activities and further strengthening its customer-centred approach. For GCB Bank, the celebration represents another opportunity to reinforce its longstanding service commitment while exploring new ways of ensuring that the customer experience extends beyond the banking hall.

items.title: GCB Bank’s Customer Experience Chief outlines wellness-driven strategy to deepen customer engagement
items.description: The Chief Marketing, Communication and Customer Experience Officer of GCB Bank PLC, Cynthia Ofori-Dwumfuo, has reaffirmed the Bank’s commitment to enhancing customer experience through wellness initiatives, digital innovation, fraud awareness and improved service delivery as part of efforts to deepen customer engagement and strengthen its customer-centred approach. The maiden Aerobics Fiesta held at the University of Ghana Stadium in Accra on Saturday, October 31, marks the grand finale of GCB Bank’s 2026 Customer Service Month celebrations, held under the theme “The Extra Mile”. The event brought together customers, employees, stakeholders and members of the public for a morning of fitness, health education and entertainment. Speaking at the event, Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo said the Bank’s commitment to customer centricity extended beyond conventional banking services to encompass the broader needs and well-being of its customers. She explained that customer service was not simply about responding to complaints or providing assistance through contact centres but involved creating meaningful experiences that strengthened relationships between the Bank and the people it serves. Customer experience beyond traditional banking A major focus of Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo’s address was the need for financial institutions to adopt a broader understanding of customer service, particularly as customer expectations continue to evolve. She stressed that delivering an excellent customer experience required more than having functional contact centres or addressing complaints. Rather, it involved understanding the different challenges customers face and ensuring that every interaction with the Bank reflected its commitment to putting customers first. “Customer service is more than just a contact centre. We know that it’s more than people calling us to complain,” she noted. She identified fraud awareness and customer protection as important aspects of the Bank’s customer-centric approach, particularly amid growing concerns about financial scams and fraudulent activities affecting banking customers. She explained that GCB Bank recognised the importance of educating customers about financial fraud while providing accessible channels through which they could obtain assistance and conduct their transactions securely. According to her, customer centricity must be reflected across the Bank’s entire service delivery structure, from its contact centre and digital platforms to its branches and interactions with employees. She highlighted the Bank’s toll-free customer service line, mobile banking application, online account opening and digital loan application services as some of the ways it was improving convenience and accessibility for customers. Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo also emphasised the importance of ensuring that employees remained responsive and intentional in their interactions with customers, noting that delivering a positive customer experience was a collective responsibility across the institution. She maintained that customer centricity remained a fundamental pillar of GCB Bank’s corporate strategy and would continue to guide its approach to service delivery and business development. Wellness takes centre stage in customer engagement Explaining the rationale behind the maiden Aerobics Fiesta, Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo said the initiative was designed to strengthen the Bank’s relationship with customers while encouraging them to take their health and general well-being seriously. She noted that the Bank wanted to create opportunities to interact with customers beyond the conventional banking environment, allowing them to connect with the institution through activities that promoted healthy living and community participation. “With this event, with this Aerobics Fiesta event, we are trying to engage with our customers on a more personal level. We are trying to encourage them to also take their wellness seriously, and what better time to do it than during Customer Service Month?” she said. The event featured aerobics sessions, yoga, breast cancer screening, prostate cancer awareness and screening, as well as a dedicated playground for children. A musical performance by Ghanaian music duo Dope Nation also provided entertainment for participants, adding to the festive atmosphere. Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo said the activities reflected the Bank’s desire to appreciate customers in ways that extended beyond the financial products and services it offered. She described the occasion as an opportunity to celebrate the people who had contributed to GCB Bank’s growth and success, including its customers, employees and stakeholders. More customer-focused initiatives expected in 2027 Looking ahead, Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo assured customers that the Bank would continue to introduce initiatives aimed at improving customer experience and strengthening its relationship with different customer groups. She indicated that GCB Bank had more customer engagement activities planned for 2027, reaffirming its commitment to becoming a more responsive and customer-focused institution. She also disclosed that the maiden Aerobics Fiesta was intended to become an annual event, with another edition expected in October 2027. “This is the first one. See you next year in October. We’ll have a similar event as well,” she announced. Her comments point to the Bank’s intention to sustain wellness and community engagement as part of its broader customer appreciation efforts. Building on a legacy of customer trust Reflecting on GCB Bank’s longstanding presence in Ghana’s financial sector, Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo expressed gratitude to the generations of customers whose loyalty and confidence had contributed to the institution’s growth since its establishment in 1953. She said the Bank remained conscious of its responsibility to serve customers across different generations, from long-standing account holders to younger customers, including members of Generation Z, as well as businesses and corporate institutions. She emphasised that maintaining the Bank’s relevance required continuous innovation and an understanding of the changing expectations of its diverse customer base. “We are truly grateful to the people who have brought us here from 1953 to every single Gen Z that has a bank account with us, whether it’s businesses or companies. We’ve been the rock of the economy of Ghana,” she said. She reiterated the Bank’s appreciation for the support it had received over the decades, adding that its ambition remained to strengthen its position as a leading financial institution while continuing to contribute to Ghana’s economic development. For Ms Ofori-Dwumfuo, the Bank’s identity as Ghana’s Bank for Life must be reflected in its ability to build lasting relationships, respond to customers’ evolving needs and deliver services that make a meaningful difference in their lives. The maiden Aerobics Fiesta therefore represented more than the conclusion of GCB Bank’s 2026 Customer Service Month. It demonstrated the institution’s intention to broaden customer engagement by bringing together financial services, wellness, digital convenience and personal interaction. As GCB Bank looks towards 2027, its focus on customer centricity, fraud awareness, digital innovation and improved service delivery is expected to remain central to its efforts to strengthen customer relationships and enhance the overall banking experience.

items.title: Opare Addo calls for greater youth participation in policy decisions at Commonwealth forum
items.description: Youth and Empowerment Minister George Opare Addo has stressed the need for young people to have a stronger voice in shaping policies and opportunities that affect their lives. He said empowering the youth to participate meaningfully in decision-making was critical to addressing their concerns and ensuring that development initiatives reflect their aspirations. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, November 3, Mr Opare Addo said discussions at the Commonwealth Youth Forum in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, had highlighted the importance of placing young people at the centre of policy development. The forum forms part of the 2026 Commonwealth Forums, which officially opened ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM). A delegation from Ghana’s Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment participated in the youth-focused gathering. According to the minister, the discussions reinforce Ghana’s commitment to creating an environment where young people can influence decisions while accessing opportunities in employment, entrepreneurship, skills development and innovation. He maintained that youth empowerment should go beyond creating opportunities for economic advancement to include giving young people a meaningful role in governance. Mr Opare Addo said Ghana’s investment in its young population remained central to building a prosperous future, emphasising that their participation and contribution were necessary for national development. The Commonwealth confirms that the 14th Commonwealth Youth Forum opened on November 2 and runs until November 4, with more than 300 youth delegates participating. This provides useful context for both stories. ￼

items.title: Spanish footballer Jesus De Miguel dies after collision with keeper
items.description: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00am (07:00 GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” his club Tenerife said in a statement. “No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.” De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball. Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel receives medical attention and gets stretchered off after a collision with FC Andorra’s Jesus Owono during the Spanish La Liga 2 match at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez in Santa Cruz de Tenerife on November 2, 2026. —Reuters Spanish police sources told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision. The incident happened towards the end of the match at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium, with the teams level at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel’s condition had “worsened neurologically”, before his death. “I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus,” former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra’s majority shareholder, wrote on social media. Andorra also sent their “most sincere condolences” to De Miguel’s family, team-mates and Tenerife. Messages of support Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the Spanish football federation (RFEF). “Shattered by this sad news, the Royal Spanish Football Federation wishes to express our deepest sorrow at his passing today,” wrote the federation in a statement. The RFEF postponed Tuesday’s matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina, “as a gesture of respect and solidarity”. European football governing body UEFA said a minute’s silence would be held before matches this week in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League. Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. “Immense sadness, there are no words,” Madrid’s French forward Kylian Mbappe wrote on Instagram. Other sports stars, including Rafa Nadal and Lionel Messi also left messages on Instagram. “There are no words… rest in peace,” wrote Inter Miami forward Messi. “What a terrible sadness… I’m with you from the bottom of my heart,” wrote Nadal. La Liga side Espanyol also delayed the presentation of their new coach Eder Sarabia until Wednesday while some clubs chose not to train. Top flight chief Javier Tebas and Spanish sports minister Milagros Tolon also posted messages of condolence. “Today we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss,” wrote Tebas on X. “We share in your grief,” wrote Tolon, offering her “deepest condolences to (De Miguel’s) family and loved ones”, as well as Tenerife, the players and staff. De Miguel had been at Tenerife for just over a season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Castellon. The striker helped the team gain promotion to the second division. The forward began his career with Leganes at youth level in the Madrid suburbs, playing for a string of teams, including Unionistas de Salamanca, before signing for Castellon in 2023.

items.description: Au Niger, 1 245 personnes ont perdu la vie dans des accidents de la route en 2025, selon les donnees de l'Agence nigerienne de securite routiere (ANISER), rapportees par l'Agence nigerienne de presse (ANP) le 2 novembre 2026. D'apres le directeur general de l'ANISER, Dr Abou Mountari, 99,24 % des accidents sont lies aux comportements humains. Les principales causes sont l'exces de vitesse (40,76 %), le refus de priorite (26,03 %) et l'imprudence (18,28 %). items.title: The world has not had a single cooler-than-normal day since December 2022
items.description: The world has gone 1,425 days in a row without a single day that was cooler than normal, the longest such run in more than 80 years of records, a JoyNews Research analysis of global temperature data shows. The last time the planet’s average temperature dipped below normal was 1 December 2022 , and even then only by 0.006°C, a difference far too small to feel. Every day since, from 2 December 2022 to 26 October 2026, has been warmer than normal for its date. The run is almost 50% longer than the previous record of 959 days, set between June 2015 and February 2018. The figures come from ERA5, a day-by-day record of the world’s weather produced by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) for the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service. JoyNews Research analysed every day from 1 January 1940 to 26 October 2026, a total of 31,711 days. What counts as “normal”? Weather experts measure “normal” as the average over 30 years. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), the United Nations’ weather agency, adopted 1991 to 2020 as the current global standard and recommends updating it every ten years. In this analysis, a day is “cooler than normal” if the world’s average temperature on that day was below the 1991–2020 average for the same date. A day in October is compared with other Octobers, not with August. By design, cooler-than-normal days should be common. In the 30 years that make up the average, about half of all days (50.6%) were below it. For nearly four years now, there has not been one. Figure 1: Every day since 2010 compared with normal. Red shows warmer-than-normal days and blue shows cooler-than-normal days. The last blue day was 1 December 2022. A record by a wide margin Long runs of warmer-than-normal days are not new. The five longest on record have all happened since 2015. But none comes close to the current one. The previous longest lasted 959 days, from 20 June 2015 to 2 February 2018. It ended with a single day just 0.05°C below normal. Another, from August 2018 to February 2021, lasted 902 days. Since the middle of 2015, the world has had only 13 cooler-than-normal days in total, and all were by small margins. The deepest was 17 February 2021, at about 0.2°C below normal. Figure 2: The five longest unbroken runs of warmer-than-normal days since 1940. All five have happened since 2015. The closest the world has come The nearest the planet came to ending the run was 14 January 2023 , when global temperature was just 0.08°C above normal. Since February 2023, the gap has never been that small: every day has been at least 0.12°C above normal. In 2026, the coolest day relative to normal was 23 February, and it was still 0.18°C warmer than usual. On average, 2026 has run 0.64°C above normal. Read also: 2026 set to be the world’s second-hottest year on record as El Niño drives August to an all-time high How the world got here A cooler-than-normal day used to be the rule, not the exception. Between 1940 and 1979, only 7 of 14,610 days were warmer than what we now call normal. In other words, more than 99.9% of days in those four decades would count as cooler than normal today. The change came steadily. In the 1990s, 88% of days were still cooler than normal. In the 2000s, it was 56%. In the 2010s,s it fell to 16%. So far in the 2020s, it is 0.4%: just ten days, and none since December 2022. 1998 was the first year in the record in which fewer than half of all days were cooler than normal. Figure 3: The share of days in each decade that were cooler than the 1991–2020 average for their date. A run that began under a cooling influence The run began while a natural cooling pattern was still in place. La Niña, which occurs when the surface of the Pacific Ocean near the equator turns unusually cool, tends to pull global temperatures down. A rare three-year La Niña was underway in December 2022. The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) declared it over on 9 March 2023. Its opposite, El Niño, then took over and helped drive 2023 and 2024 to back-to-back global temperature records. Another El Niño is now underway. NOAA said on 8 October that a key Pacific temperature index stood at 2.1°C above normal and gave a more than 83% chance of a strong to very strong El Niño lasting into early 2027. Measured against older “normals,” the run is even longer. Because the reference period moves forward every ten years, “normal” itself is getting warmer. Compared with the previous standard, 1981 to 2010, the world’s last cooler-than-normal day was 4 March 2014 , more than 12 years ago. When the WMO moves to the next reference period, the bar is expected to rise again. The run of warmer-than-normal days would then look shorter on paper, even though the world itself would not be any cooler. What it means for Ghana These are global averages and do not describe conditions in any single country. But Ghana is feeling the same pressure. In its outlook for the September to November minor rainy season, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) forecast warmer-than-normal temperatures across most of the country. Scientists link a warmer baseline to more frequent and more intense heatwaves and to heavier downpours when rain does fall. In the 1940s, every single day was cooler than what we now call normal. Today, the world cannot manage even one.
